name: Anderson Butte Lookout
loc:
Nez Perce National Forest 
                    Idaho County, Idaho
desc: The first lookout was a tent camp posted on Idaho’s Anderson Butte in 1914. In the early 1930s, an L-4 lookout was placed on the summit on a short tower. The current structure, an L-4 with catwalk on a 53’ timber tower, was built in 1953 and is staffed on an emergency basis. It is the last lookout of its type on the Nez Perce National Forest.

name: Arctic Point Lookout
loc:
Payette National Forest 
                    Idaho County, Idaho
desc:
Possibly the most remote active lookout in the continental United States, Arctic Point Fire Lookout has been retired to standby status. The 72’ Aermotor tower with metal 7’ x 7’ cab atop a 7,516' mountain in Idaho’s Payette National Forest was constructed in 1935. A Rocky Mountain-style log cabin ground house was added in 1939. Reached only by foot or horseback on an 18 mile trail, it was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1994. 
 Payette National Forest - September 2020:  
 
 The Forest Service used the lookout primarily for seasonal fire watch. However, during WWII, it was used to look for Japanese Balloon Bombs. These were hydrogen inflated balloons with incendiary devices attached to them. These balloons were dispersed from Japan between November 1944 and April 1945 with the hopes that atmospheric winds would carry them to US forests. Japan launched more than 9,000 of these weapons to cause wildfires. Since 1997, the lookout has remained unstaffed and was placed on the National Register of Historic Places.

name: Arid Peak Lookout
loc:
Idaho Panhandle National Forest 
                    Shoshone County, Idaho
desc: The lookout on Arid Peak was placed within a roadless area overlooking the Milwaukee Road Railroad to provide early detection of train fires.  The 20’ L-4 hip-roof cab with catwalk was built in 1931 and the tower legs replaced in 1969. Although this Idaho Panhandle National Forest lookout has not been staffed for 25 years, the structure is solid enough for restoration, which is slated to begin in 1996.

name: Austin Ridge Lookout
loc:
Clearwater National Forest 
                    Idaho County, Idaho
desc: The original Austin Ridge Lookout on the Clearwater National Forest was an L-4 on 30' pole tower. It was replaced in 1960 with this 15'x15' R-6 cab with catwalk on a 53' timber tower. Staffed until the early 1990s, it was formerly in the rental program but is now inactive.

name: Bald Mountain Lookout
loc:
Clearwater National Forest 
                    Latah County, Idaho
desc: The first facility on Bald Mountain Hill Lookout was a cabin built in 1913 which was replaced with an L-4 cab on a 50’ pole tower in 1938. This R-6 flattop cab with catwalk on a 41’ timber tower was built in 1960. Refurbished in 1998, it is on the Clearwater National Forest cabin rental program.

name: Basin Butte Lookout
loc:
Salmon-Challis National Forest 
                    Custer County, Idaho
desc: Perched high in the Salmon River Mountains on the Salmon-Challis National Forest, Basin Butte Lookout was built in 1934. In emergency only status for a number of years, this 14’x14’ L-4 groundhouse with catwalk was completely restored in 2008 with a volunteer Passport in Time project by the USFS.

name: Bear Creek Point Lookout
loc:
Salmon-Challis National Forest 
                    Valley County, Idaho
desc: Located within the famed River of No Return Wilderness, Bear Creek Point Lookout is reached only by trail. The L-5 10’x10’ groundhouse was abandoned in the 1950s.

name: Bear Mountain Lookout
loc:
Clearwater National Forest 
                    Idaho County, Idaho
desc: A classic example of the L-4 cab with catwalk, Bear Mountain Lookout is on 53’ timber tower built in 1951. It replaced an L-6 cab on a 45’ pole tower dating to 1935 and the 1922 Clearwater National Forest log cabin which is still there.

name: Bear Valley Lookout
loc:
Frank Church River of No Return Wilderness 
                    Valley County, Idaho
desc: Located within the River of No Return Wilderness in the Boise National Forest, Bear Valley Lookout is a 7'x7' metal cab on a 46' steel tower. It is maintained for emergency use.

name: Beartrap Lookout
loc:
Salmon-Challis National Forest 
                    Lemhi County, Idaho
desc:
The first Beartrap Lookout on the Salmon National Forestwas a log cabin built in 1919. In 1935 this L-4 with catwalk on a log crib was built. 
 It burned in the August 2012 Mustang complex fire.

name: Beaver Ridge Lookout
loc:
Clearwater National Forest 
                    Idaho County, Idaho
desc: The R-6 flat cab with catwalk on a 12’ concrete base is only the second Beaver Ridge Lookout on the Clearwater National Forest. The first at this site was a log cupola cabin built by the Forest Service in 1922.

name: Bertha Hill Lookout
loc: Clearwater County, Idaho
desc:
Bertha Hill Lookout, owned by the Clearwater-Potlatch Timber Protective Association in Idaho, has considerable historical importance. The site of one of the first lookouts in the West, and the first lookout in Idaho, Bertha Hill is considered to be the birthplace of cooperative forest fire protection. The first lookout was posted in 1900, well before state and federal programs were established. The original lookout was a simple pole ladder to a seat on a large limb. Mable Gray, the camp cook at Bertha Hill timber camp 1/8 mile down the east sleep, rode her horse to the tree and sat on the limb daily after doing the morning dishes. 
 In 1906, the Clearwater Timber Protective Assocation established a crude open pole platform atop three cut-off fir trees 100 feet south of the original lookout tree. It was replaced in 1910 by a 37' crude open pole platform adjacent to the 1906 tower. 
 A 20' pole tower with an enclosed 6'x6' cab was built in 1918. Lookout Glen Frazier was killed by lightning while on duty in this tower in 1931. It was replaced in 1933 by a 40' pole L-4 tower built at a slightly different location atop Bertha Hill's main summit. 
 The current 56-ft steel tower, with a 14- by 14-ft live-in cab, is the fifth to be located on the site. It was constructed in 1959 and includes a public observation platform at the 46-ft level. Lookout Maida Talbot died in a fall from the tower in 1966.

name: Big Soldier Lookout
loc:
Salmon-Challis National Forest 
                    Custer County, Idaho
desc: First used as a lookout with a tent camp in 1934, Big Soldier Lookout was constructed in 1934. The 14’x14’ groundhouse with a catwalk supported with poles has been inactive for many years. It is within the River of No Return Wilderness.

name: Big Springs Lookout
loc:
Targhee National Forest 
                    Fremont County, Idaho

name: Bishop Mountain Lookout
loc:
Targhee National Forest 
                    Fremont County, Idaho
desc: Bishop Mountain Lookout is one of the few remaining towers on the Targhee National Forest in Idaho. The 72-ft steel Aermotor tower, with a 7- by 7-ft cab, was constructed in 1937. Now on standby status, the tower saw extensive service during the Yellowstone Fires of 1988.

name: Black Mountain Lookout
loc:
Clearwater National Forest 
                    Clearwater County, Idaho
desc: In use since the 1930s, Black Mountain Lookout is the third structure on this site in the Clearwater National Forest. It is a 14'x14' modified R-6 flattop cab with catwalk on a 10’ concrete block base and remains in active service.

name: Blue Nose Lookout
loc:
Salmon-Challis National Forest 
                    Lemhi County, Idaho
desc: One of the few remaining 2-story long log crib lookouts with an L-4 cab, Blue Nose Lookout on the Salmon National Forest is maintained by volunteers.

name: Burnt Knob Lookout
loc:
Nez Perce National Forest 
                    Idaho County, Idaho
desc: Burnt Knob Lookout’s name reflects the fire history of the area. Located on the edge of the Selway Bitterroot Wilderness in the Nez Perce National Forest, the site was first used in 1922 when an alidade was placed on the summit. The unique L-5 log lookout cabin was built in 1930 and staffed until the 1960s. It is maintained for emergency use.

name: Burton Peak Lookout
loc:
Idaho Panhandle (Kaniksu) National Forests 
                    Boundary County, Idaho
desc: The only remaining L-5 log frame lookout house in North Idaho, Burton Peak Lookout was built in 1933, abandoned in 1967 and is showing its age. The historic structure has had emergency repairs by volunteers.

name: Butts Creek Point Lookout
loc:
Salmon-Challis National Forest 
                    Idaho County, Idaho
desc: Built in 1934, this L-4 cab rests on a foundation made of log cribbing. Due to its remote location, requiring a boat to cross the Salmon River and a 6-mile hike with over 5,000 feet of elevation gain, this tower is rarely visited. It is believed to have been staffed during the 1960s and 1970s.   Twice a year, former lookout Dr. Phillip Krueger of Boise, Idaho, visits the lookout to open and close it for the season.

name: Carey Dome Fire Lookout
loc:
Payette National Forest 
                    Idaho County, Idaho
desc: The last active fire tower on the Fayette National Forest, Carey Dome Lookout was placed into service in 1934. The 721 Aermotor tower with 7’ x 7’ metal cab is eligible for the National Register of Historic Sites. The observer’s residence is a Rocky Mountain style log cabin.

name: Castle Butte Lookout
loc:
Clearwater National Forest 
                    Idaho County, Idaho
desc: Castle Butte Lookout went into service on the Clearwater National Forest as a frame cabin in 1916. In 1928 it was replaced with an R-1 log cabin with cupola. The present 14’x14’ L-4 cab with catwalk on a 10’ stone base was built in 1950. Recently rehabbed, it is now in the recreation rental system.

name: Chair Point Lookout
loc:
Nez Perce National Forest 
                    Idaho County, Idaho
desc: The first structure at Chair Point Lookout on the Nez Perce National Forest was a log cabin which is still there. The accompanying 45’ log tower with a L-6 cab was replaced in 1953 with an L-4 cab on a 41’ timber tower. The present R-6 flat cab with catwalk on a 41’ timber tower went into service in 1980.

name: Chicken Peak Lookout
loc:
Payette National Forest 
                    Idaho County, Idaho
desc: One of the last lookouts in the Frank Church - River of No Return Wilderness on the Payette National Forest in central Idaho, Chicken Peak is a cultural treasure needing care. It is the only known remaining example of this style of pre-CCC log and timber cab and the oldest lookout on the forest. The 14' x 14' R4-D8 cab with steep pyramid roof and no catwalk was built in 1930 and staffed until 1969.

name: Clarke Mountain Lookout
loc:
Clearwater National Forest 
                    Clearwater County, Idaho
desc: The first lookout was in the 1920s with a D-6 cupola cabin. The present L-4 cab atop a 10' concrete base was built in 1952.

name: Cold Mountain Lookout
loc:
Payette National Forest 
                    Valley County, Idaho
desc: This lookout was built in 1935 with materials hauled in over a hundred miles by pack mule over trails into the Payette National Forest. In 1936 a log cabin was constructed on site. The following year a young Norman Borlaug (winner of a Nobel Prize in 1974), staffed the 72’ Aermotor tower with 7’x7’ metal cab. The tower was removed in 1994 and the cabin burned by a wildfire in 2000. In 2007 a private party restored the top 20’ of the tower near the shore of Payette Lake.

name: Conrad Peak Lookout
loc:
Idaho Panhandle National Forest 
                    Shoshone County, Idaho
desc: Conrad Peak Lookout, at 50’, is the tallest lookout tower remaining on the St. Joe River drainage in the Idaho Panhandle National Forest. Constructed in 1955, the L-4 hip-roof cab with catwalk replaced a log cupola lookout built in 1931.  It is no longer used for fire detection.

name: Coolwater Lookout
loc:
Nez Perce National Forest 
                    Idaho County, Idaho
desc: The original Coolwater Lookout on the Nez Perce National Forest was a 12’x12’ frame cabin built in 1915, and replaced by a 14’x14’ log cabin in 1931. In 1936 a gable-roof L-4 was built on the summit, and then moved 100’ in 1953 to make room for the current hip-roof L-4 with catwalk on a 10’ wood tower.

name: Corral Hill Lookout
loc:
Nez Perce National Forest 
                    Idaho County, Idaho
desc: Corral Hill Lookout went into service in 1929 as a 40’ pole tower with a tent cabin at the base. In 1953 the Nez Perce National Forest constructed this L-4 cab with catwalk on a 41’ timber tower.

name: Custer Lookout
loc:
Salmon-Challis National Forest 
                    Custer County, Idaho
desc: Built in 1933, Custer Lookout is one of very few R-5 C-3 cabs in Idaho. The design dates to 1917 and is a precursor to the popular L-4 developed in the early 1930s. It is a 14’x14’ groundhouse with catwalk.

name: Deadwood Lookout
loc:
Boise National Forest 
                    Boise County, Idaho
desc: With a 10 year restoration effort recently completed, Deadwood Lookout on the Boise National Forest looks much as it did the day it went into service in 1936, replacing a cupola lookout built in 1924. This CCC structure was active for many years but is now on standby status and is available for rental.

name: Deer Ridge Lookout
loc:
Idaho Panhandle (Kaniksu) National Forests 
                    Boundary County, Idaho
desc: The Deer Ridge Lookout is a 41’ tall 15’x15’ R-6 fl attop with catwalk built in 1965. It was preceded by an L-4 on a 20’ pole tower (1935) and an L-4 on a 40’ timber tower (1949). It is located on the Idaho Panhandle National Forest and is in the cabin rental system.

name: Diablo Lookout
loc:
Clearwater National Forest 
                    Idaho County, Idaho
desc: Located in the Selway-Bitterroot Wilderness on the Clearwater National Forest, Diablo Lookout is an R-6 cab with catwalk on a 10’ concrete base built in 1965. It replaced a gable roof L-4 ground cab built in 1926.

name: Dry Diggins Lookout
loc:
Nez Perce National Forest 
                    Idaho County, Idaho
desc: The original lookout, built in 1932 one mile southeast of the current site, was an L-4 cab which blew away in 1967. The present 10' concrete base with R-6 cab, built in 1968, is available for emergencies.

name: Duck Creek Point Lookout
loc:
Salmon-Challis National Forest 
                    Lemhi County, Idaho
desc: Built in 1935 on the Salmon-Challis National Forest, Duck Creek Point Lookout is a 10'x10' cab similar to an L-5. Originally a ground house, a 9' log base was added in 1944. No longer staffed, it received a new roof in 2004.

name: Dunn Peak Lookout
loc:
St. Joe National Forest 
                    Shoshone County, Idaho
desc: Dunn Peak lookout doesn't appear to be used as a lookout anymore. It now houses communication equipment.

name: East Mountain Lookout
loc: Valley County, Idaho
admin: Southern Idaho Timber Protective Association, Inc.
desc: East Mountain Lookout is the first of the unique Idaho log house lookouts to be listed in the NHLR. Very few remain in existence. The first was a two-story 18’ x 18’ hip-roof structure built in 1914 by the Southern Idaho Timber Protective Association. It was replaced in the 1930s by a similar 20’x20’ log house lookout by a CCC crew under the direction of two Finnish carpenters. The lookout was staffed through 1995, when it was decommissioned. It is located on the Boise National Forest.   A dry lightening storm moved across the area in late June/early July, 2002 and started a 5 acre fire on the east side of the lookout, and strong winds carried small bits of flaming material uphill toward the lookout, which caught fire and burnt down before help arrived. The lookout was in the final stages of restoration by a preservation group when the fire occurred.

name: Elk Butte Lookout
loc: Clearwater County, Idaho
desc: Elk Butte Lookout is one of two remaining active lookouts operated by the Clearwater-Potlatch Timber Protective Association in North Idaho. It is one of two “lookout within a lookout” towers known in the U.S. Strangely, both are named for elk. (The other is Elk Neck in Maryland). The 80’ WWII surplus steel tower was erected in 1948 with a metal 7’x7’ cab. The wooden live-in cab from the earlier 1933 tower has been maintained at the 30’ level.

name: Elk Summit Lookout
loc:
Nez Perce National Forest 
                    Idaho County, Idaho
desc: One of only four active Aermotor lookouts remaining in the USFS Northern Region, Elk Summit has been a lookout site since a crow’s nest observation point was established there in 1911. The 100’ tower with 7’ x 7’ cab was built in 1934 and is still used on an as-needed basis by the Elk City Ranger District of the Nez Perce National Forest.

name: Eyeful Tower Lookout
loc: Idaho County, Idaho
desc: Originally erected on Sawyer Ridge in Idaho’s Nez Perce National Forest in 1949, this 41’ timber tower with a 14’ x 14’ L-4 hip roof cab and catwalk was declared surplus to Forest Service needs in 1987. It was purchased by Bruce & Nancy Dreher (Bruce is retired from the Forest Service) and reconstructed next to their home overlooking the Slate Creek Ranger Station. Faithfully restored and renamed the “Eyeful Tower,” tours are available by pre-arrangement.

name: Gardiner Peak Lookout
loc:
Nez Perce National Forest 
                    Idaho County, Idaho
desc: The standard 1936-model hip-roof L-4 cab lookout with catwalk on a 10’ wooden tower at Gardiner Peak Lookout on the Nez Perce National Forest was built in 1953. It replaced an L-3 cupola cabin on a 5’ log crib constructed in 1925. Gardiner Peak sits above the Selway River within the Selway-Bitterroot Wilderness Area on the boundary between the Nez Perce National Forest and the Bitterroot National Forest.  Gardiner is regularly staffed for fire detection.

name: Gisborne Mountain Lookout
loc:
Idaho Panhandle National Forests 
                    Bonner County, Idaho
desc: Originally known as Looking Glass Mountain, Gisborne Mountain Lookout was renamed for Harry T. Gisborne who conducted fire research on the surrounding Priest River Experimental Forest (a part of the Kaniksu National Forest). The first lookout was built in 1932, with the present 41’ wooden tower with 15x15’ live-in flattop cab and catwalk being constructed in 1958.

name: Granite Mountain Lookout
loc:
Salmon National Forest 
                    Lemhi County, Idaho
desc: The classic L-4 live-in lookout at Granite Mountain on the Salmon National Forest was constructed by the Forest Service in 1934. Active for 30 years, it went on standby status in 1960s. It was completely and carefully restored in 2002 by the North Fork Ranger District with assistance of North Fork Volunteer Fire Dept., Passport In Time, and the Forest Heritage staff.

name: Grave Peak Lookout
loc:
Clearwater National Forest 
                    Idaho County, Idaho
desc: Grave Peak Lookout is the only D-6 cupola-style structure in the Selway-Bitteroot Wilderness—Clearwater National Forest—and one of the three remaining in Northern Idaho and Montana. The 8,062’ peak was first used in 1914 for fire detection and the 12’x12’ groundhouse was constructed in 1924. The site was featured in a story recounted in the book: “A River Runs Through It” by Norman McLean, who worked as a lookout on Grave Peak in 1919.

name: Grave Point Lookout
loc:
Nez Perce National Forest 
                    Idaho County, Idaho
desc: Grave Point Lookout overlooks both the Salmon River and the Hells Canyon on the Nez Perce National Forest. The 41’ timber tower with a 1936-model L-4 cab with catwalk was built in 1954, replacing a log cupola cabin built in 1924.  Grave Point sits above both the Salmon River and the Hells Canyon area of the Snake River. The lookout was used as a site for hacking falcons for several years.

name: Green Mountain Lookout
loc:
Nez Perce National Forest 
                    Idaho County, Idaho
desc: Located six miles northwest of Burnt Knob in the Nez Perce National Forest is Green Mountain Lookout. The first lookout on the site was a cabin built in 1930. The current L-4 tower with catwalk was constructed in 1956. While not regularly staffed since the early 1970s, it is frequently used on an emergency basis given the high fire frequency of the area.

name: Heavens Gate Lookout
loc:
Nez Perce National Forest 
                    Idaho County, Idaho
desc: Heaven’s Gate Lookout was so named to counter the fact that it looks over the Seven Devils and the Hells Canyon area of the Nez Perce National Forest. The original 1924 log cabin with cupola was destroyed in a 1958 fire.  Twenty years later this R-6 flattop with catwalk on a 10’ stone base was constructed. Heavens Gate was reportedly named in contrast to the nearby Seven Devils and Hells Canyon. Heavens Gate Lookout is currently administered by the Hells Canyon National Recreation Area and has been staffed in most recent years.

name: Hell's Half Acre Lookout
loc:
Bitterroot National Forest 
                    Idaho County, Idaho
desc: In 1930 Hell’s Half Acre Lookout on the Bitterroot National Forest was a platform on a 40’ tree top. In 1940 it was replaced by an L-4 cab on a 10’ tower, which in turn was replaced 20 years later by this R-6 flattop catwalk on a 10’ concrete base. From its spot four air miles south of the Montana Road in the Magruder Corridor, Hell's Half Acre Lookout overlooks the upper reaches of the Selway River in the adjacent Frank Church River of No Return Wilderness. It is regularly staffed during the fire season.

name: Hemlock Butte Lookout
loc:
Clearwater National Forest 
                    Idaho/Clearwater County Line, Idaho
desc: Still in service on the Clearwater National Forest, Hemlock Butte Lookout is a 14’x14’ L-4 cab with catwalk on a 54’ tower built in 1954. Previous lookouts art the site were a roofed platform (1919), D-6 cupola cabin (1923), and an L-4 on a 50’ pole tower (1934).

name: Hidden Peak Lookout
loc:
Lolo/Clearwater National Forests 
                    Idaho County, Idaho
desc: Built in 1927, the first lookout was a 16'x16' shake cabin. An L-4 cab replaced it in 1931. The present 10' concrete base topped by an R-6 cab, built in 1961, was used for emergencies into the 1970s. Open to public use, the site is located in the Selway-Bitterroot Wilderness.

name: Horton Peak Lookout
loc: Custer County, Idaho

name: Hughes Ridge Lookout
loc:
Idaho Panhandle National Forests 
                    Boundary County, Idaho
desc:
The only remaining L-R tower in Boundary County, Idaho, Hughes Ridge Lookout is located in a remote corner of the Idaho Panhandle National Forests inhabited by woodland caribou and grizzly bears. The 41’ wooden tower has a 14’ x 14’ live-in cab and catwalk. 
 Lookout Vern Marschall staffed this lookout during the summers of 1965 and 1966.

name: Indian Hill Lookout
loc:
Nez Perce National Forest 
                    Idaho County, Idaho
desc: The first Indian Hill Lookout structure was a 14’x16’ log cabin built in 1929 on the Nez Perce National Forest and still standing. The current L-4 cab with catwalk on a 41 timber tower was constructed in 1951, replacing an L-6 cab on a 45’ pole tower that had been built in 1930.

name: Indian Mountain Lookout
loc:
Payette National Forest 
                    Adams County, Idaho
desc: The only lookout of its type constructed on the Payette National Forest, Indian Mountain is a R1/L4 structure with 14’x 14’ cab and catwalk. It was built in 1933, replacing a cupola cabin dating from 1922, and restored to original specifications in 1993-94. Still in active service, the site was first used for detection in 1910 with a tent camp.

name: Junction Mountain Lookout
loc:
Clearwater National Forest 
                    Clearwater County, Idaho
desc: This 53-foot tall L-4 tower is constructed of treated lumber. The windows and bottom stairs have been removed. Previously, a 1931 tower featuring a log crib foundation was on this site.

name: Little Guard Lookout
loc:
Idaho Panhandle National Forest 
                    Shoshone County, Idaho
desc: Little Guard Lookout is located northwest of Interstate 90 and Lookout Pass on the Coeur d'Alene National Forest in Idaho. The 14- by 14-ft. live-in cab, on a 10-ft. concrete block base, was constructed in 1956. It replaced a wooded cupola-type lookout built in 1929. The lookout is still manned and maintained by the Wallace Ranger District.

name: Little Snowy Top Lookout
loc:
Idaho Panhandle National Forests 
                    Boundary County, Idaho
desc:
Little Snowy Top is the only remaining 1930s vintage groundhouse L-4 lookout in the Priest Lake area of northern Idaho. Located only two miles south of the Canadian border, its use was phased out in the 1960s, but it escaped demolition due to its remote location (a nine-mile trail). In 1987 volunteers from the Spokane Mountaineers and the Priest River Back Country Horsemen assisted the Priest Lake Ranger District of the Idaho Panhandle National Forests in a two-year restoration effort of the 14’x 14’ groundhouse. 
 The tower was destroyed in a September 3, 2016 fire.

name: Little Soldier Lookout
loc:
Salmon Challis National Forest 
                    Custer County, Idaho
desc:
Located in the northwest corner of the Challis National Forest and overlooking the River of No Return Wilderness, Little Soldier lookout was built in 1934. The 14’x14’ hip roof L-4 groundhouse with catwalk was on emergency status for a number of years but is again in active service.
 

 
The interior of the tower features a cirle fire finder atop a wooden stand in the middle of the floor. The windows on all four sides are comprised of windowpane sections. On the north side of the room is a wood shelf that holds the  table radio. There is a black wood stove, and built-in shelves on the opposite side of the room.  There are four heavy wood shutters raised and anchored to the deck by rebar-like structures.  There is a small door on the south side of the structure. A wood deck wraps around the four sides of the lookout. Several old cement steps lead down to a wood hitching post. A small  wood shed, and an outhouse comprise the other structures at the site. 
 

 
Since Little Soldier is at a lower elevation, there are pine trees in close proximity, and the hillsides are covered in mountains grasses and sage.  The main trail leading to the lookout is a steep ten mile ascent of deeply rutted switchbacks from the Indian Creek Ranger Station on the Middle Fork of the Salmon River via foot/horseback.  There is a ridge trail that leads to a water pipe in a grove of thick pines that's frequented by wildlife and used as a game trail.  The trail passes by the lookout, and it's common to see game near the deck. There's a long sloping saddle at the south side of the site and vast mountain ranges for as far as the eye can see in every direction. It's a 'remote' lookout with no road access.  Fire lookout personnel must pack provisions in for the entire season. L.S. lookout is a peaceful and serene setting. 
 

 
Lookout Christa Everett staffed this site in 1988 and 1989.

name: Lookout Butte Lookout
loc:
Nez Perce National Forest 
                    Idaho County, Idaho
desc: A 45’ pole tower served as the first Lookout Butte Lookout on the Nez Perce National Forest in 1923 with a cab added in 1925. A 50’ pole tower with L-4 cab was built in 1935 and replaced with the current 15’x15’ R-6 fl at top cab with catwalk on a 55’ timber tower in 1962. It is now available in the rental program.

name: Lookout Mountain Lookout
loc: Boundary County, Idaho
desc: Lookout Mountain, Idaho was first used for fire detection in 1921 with the cupola structure completed in 1929. It was supplemented with a CCC-built L4 tower in 1939. The mountain was abandoned as an active fire detection site in 1947 and the tower collapsed around 1965. In 1977 a steel tower was moved from Packsaddle Lookout and topped with a 12 x 12 wooden cab by the Idaho Dept. of Lands. The original cupola structure--one of only two of its type left--was restored in 1983-1992.

name: Lookout Mountain Lookout
loc:
Sawtooth National Recreation Area 
                    Custer County, Idaho
desc: This L-4 ground cab lookout was restored in 1989 by a former 1961 lookout staff member. In 1985 it was to be burned and he contacted the Forest Service.  He repaired the hardwood floors, door, two shutters, catwalk, and steps.  It was also painted. There appear to be some recent improvements based on the tools/supplies inside the lookout.

name: Lunch Peak Lookout
loc:
Idaho Panhandle National Forests 
                    Bonner County, Idaho
desc: Lunch Peak Lookout is the last modern day lookout on the Sandpoint District of the Idaho Panhandle National Forests. The first lookout on the site was a hip roof L-4 cab on a 50’ pole tower built in 1937. In 1971 the current 15’x15’ flattop cab with catwalk on a 10’ concrete base was constructed and remained in service until 1985. The lookout is now in the cabin rental program and will be listed in the National Lookout Register until it is 50 years old.

name: Mahoney Creek Point Lookout
loc:
Boise/Challis National Forests 
                    Valley County, Idaho
desc: Mahoney Creek Lookout on the Challis National Forest is an L-4 ground house built in 1937. It is now an abandoned orphan needing adoption.

name: Mallard Peak Lookout
loc:
Idaho Panhandle National Forest 
                    Shoshone County, Idaho
desc:
Mallard Peak Lookout was one of the 1929 prototypes from which the successful L-4 cab evolved (thousands were later produced in prefab kits suitable for delivery by mule packstrings). It was built by a ranger and his crew on the old Pole Mountain Ranger District of the St. Joe National Forest (both names are now gone and merged into adjacent units). Located on the boundary between the Clearwater and Idaho Panhandle National Forests within a proposed wilderness, Mallard Peak was last staffed in 1956. In 1981 Ray Kresek and Don Mathis completed the initial stabilization of the structure. Since 1992 the Inland Empire Llama Association has provided annual maintenance.
 

 
Restoration information from Stephan E. Matz, Heritage Manager of Idaho Panhandle NF:  "Thanks to Richard Fuller, the Grubham family (Tim, Carrie, Kyle, Britta, Cammie and Madison), Gary Weber,  Destry Scheel, Chuck Mark and a generous donation of paint and supplies from the FFLA we got quite a bit of work accomplished this last weekend at Mallard Peak Lookout, including:  All shutters are in place (the two gabled ends have working shutters, while the two sides are nailed or screwed in place); All siding, most of the trim and the two south end window shutters and the door shutter are painted white (we did not paint shutters that will be replaced); Cans were flattened and placed over woodpecker holes on the south end and painted white; Gary put most of the lightening protection system back together (we need new clamps on the southeast corner); etached southeast guy wire (the consensus was that the large flat boulder the guy is attached to may be sliding slightly down hill causing the corner to pull away); The corner was pulled back in line and since there wasn't enough wood to successfully nail to (the sill over the door had been ripped to provide sufficient room for installation of the new door) Tim nailed a length of wood into the space above the door and screwed a galvanized hinge across the corner to hold it temporarily in place; and Tim used his fall arrest equipment to do minor repairs to the roof and the stove chimney pipe.  I took extensive notes and photos of the lookout and collected samples of hinges and materials for next year's project.  I left the new interpretive notebook and took all but the most recent lookout logs so that they can be copied and put on the web this winter.  I will take them back up next trip.  I will pull together some additional plans for restoration in the near future and send them out to everyone. We are also working on a Mallard Web Page that should be ready in the next week or two.  I will let everyone know when it is done.  Thanks again for everyone's help and especially to  Richard for his enthusiasm, donation of materials and tools and efforts in keeping the project moving forward, to Tim for his expertise, donation of materials and family who painted the majority of the lookout, and Gary Weber for his expertise and FFLA connections and supplies donation.  We certainly can not forget Don Mathis and Ray Kresek for their early efforts at restoration, moral support, information about the lookout and Ray's offer of materials for this year's work.  Destry Scheel made sure our temporary shutters were helicoptered in.  I also appreciate that Chuck Mark, the District Ranger, thought enough of the project to come up on his weekend off to help out and his offer of support for next year's work."

name: McConnell Lookout
loc:
Clearwater National Forest 
                    Idaho County, Idaho
desc: McConnell Lookout is also located in the Selway-Bitteroot Wilderness -- Clearwater National Forest -- and consists of two log structures. The spot was used as a lookout site in 1918 and the one-room 14’x 14’ cabin living quarters was built in a meadow 450 yards northwest of the summit. In 1935 a 6’ x 6’ log cupola was constructed atop McConnell Mountain.

name: Meadow Creek Lookout
loc:
Boise National Forest 
                    Valley County, Idaho
desc: This L-4 14'x14' ground cab, built in 1933, is available for emergencies.

name: Middle Fork Peak Lookout
loc:
Salmon National Forest 
                    Lemhi County, Idaho
desc: Built in 1929, the first lookout on this site was a DuBois cabin. This was replaced in 1962 with the present 10' concrete base with R-6 flat cab, which is staffed in the summer.

name: Middle Sister Peak Lookout
loc:
Idaho Panhandle National Forest 
                    Shoshone County, Idaho
desc: The first lookout on Middle Sister Peak located in the Idaho Panhandle National Forest was a log cupola cabin built in 1923. It was replaced in 1951 with a L-4 lookout atop a 35’ tower which accidentally burned two years later. The present 30’ L-4 cab atop a 30’ tower with dimension timber legs was built in 1954 and remained active until 1989. Since 1992 it has been staffed and restored by volunteers.

name: Oreana Lookout
loc:
Salmon-Challis National Forest 
                    Lemhi County, Idaho
desc: Oreana Lookout is an L-4 cab with catwalk built on a one story log crib in 1934. Located on the Salmon-Challis National Forest it survived the 2011 Saddle Complex wildfire through the actions of a fire crew.

name: Oregon Butte Lookout
loc:
Nez Perce National Forest 
                    Idaho County, Idaho
desc: Oregon Butte Lookout received its name because of the clear view of Oregon’s Wallowa Mountains from its summit. The first lookout was a tent camp in the 1920s, soon replaced by a log cupola cabin in 1929. The current R6 flattop in a 7 concrete base was constructed in 1963. Located in the Gospel Hump Wilderness in the Nez Perce National Forest and reached by a five-mile trail, it remains a primary lookout and is staffed every season.

name: Osier Ridge Lookout
loc:
Clearwater National Forest 
                    Clearwater County, Idaho
desc: In 1921 the Clearwater National Forest built a pole platform tower and a ground cabin at Osier Ridge Lookout, which was replaced with a 40’ pole tower with L-4 cab in 1938. This 15’x15’ R-6 fl at top cab with catwalk on a 40’ timber tower was built in 1961 and is still active.

name: Peck Mountain Lookout
loc:
Payette National Forest 
                    Adams County, Idaho
desc: The first lookout on Peck Mountain in the Payette National Forest was a roofed 6' x 6' platform with a 6' x 8' ground house. It was constructed by the Southern Idaho Timber Protective Association. In 1935 the CCC constructed the 74' Aermotor steel tower with a 7' x 7' metal cab, along with a ground cabin and garage. The topped tree survives next to the tower.

name: Pilot Knob Lookout
loc:
Nez Perce National Forest 
                    Idaho County, Idaho
desc: The first structure at Pilot Knob Lookout was a 10’x10’ frame cabin built in 1922. This classic 1932 model hip roof  L-4 cab on a 10’ tower was built in 1939. Still in service on the Nez Perce National Forest, is it one of the few with a Bosworth fire finder. The lookout is regularly staffed every year.

name: Pilot Peak Lookout
loc:
Boise National Forest 
                    Boise County, Idaho
desc: Built on the Boise National Forest in 1932, Pilot Peak Lookout is an L-4 cab with catwalk on a concrete base and in active use.

name: Pinyon Peak Lookout
loc:
Salmon Challis National Forest 
                    Custer County, Idaho
desc: Built in 1930 Pinyon Peak lookout has been in active service since that time. The 14’x14’ hip roof L-4 groundhouse with catwalk is on a peak nearly 10,000’ high.  It is on the Challis National Forest.

name: Rice Peak Lookout
loc:
Boise National Forest 
                    Valley County, Idaho
desc: Started as a camp lookout in 1916, the first structure built was a log cupola cabin in 1922. The present L-4 ground cab on cement foundation, built in 1940, has not been used for several years.

name: Rock Rabbit Fire Lookout
loc:
Payette National Forest 
                    Idaho County, Idaho
desc: The first lookout facility on Rock Rabbit Mountain (1929) consisted of a tent camp and tree platform (which remains today). In 1937 the Rocky Mountain style log cabin and a 46' Aermotor steel tower with 7' x 7' cab were added. The tower was removed in 1981 but the other structures remain. The site is within the Frank Church-River of No Return Wilderness on the Payette National Forest.

name: Rocky Point Lookout
loc:
Clearwater National Forest 
                    Idaho County, Idaho
desc: Located on the historic Lolo Indian Trail used by Lewis & Clark in the Clearwater National Forest, Rocky Point Lookout  is an R-6 flattop with catwalk on a 10’ concrete base built in 1963. It replaced an L-4 cab on a 10’ long crib built in 1934. With relatively easy access from Powell, Rocky Point Lookout is regularly staffed every year.

name: Rocky Point Lookout
loc:
Payette National Forest 
                    Idaho County, Idaho
desc:
This lookout was a one-of-a-kind log structure designed and built by the Payette National Forest in 1937. The 15’x15’ cabin, with dovetailed corners, was built entirely with hand tools with logs collected on site. Inactive since 1945, the windows were removed in the 1960s and the historic lookout abandoned to the elements.
 

 
The lookout burned during the summer of 2015.

name: Ruffneck Peak Lookout
loc:
Salmon Challis National Forest 
                    Custer County, Idaho
desc: The most western lookout on the Challis National Forest, Ruffneck Peak is a hip roof L-4 groundhouse with catwalk. Built in 1932 and staffed until the 1980’s, it was returned to active service in 2001.

name: Rush Creek Point Lookout
loc:
Payette National Forest 
                    Valley County, Idaho
desc: Built by the Civilian Conservation Corps in 1937 in what is now designated as the Frank Church-River of No Return Wilderness within the Payette National Forest in central Idaho, Rush Creek Point Lookout is an unusual structure. Similar to an L4, it is actually an R4 plan #80 15' x 15' cab fitted with a pyramid roof. Rehabilitated once and used only by wilderness patrols since 1986, the lookout is still in reasonably good condition. But it does need maintenance. Access is only by trail.

name: Sagebrush Lookout
loc:
Salmon-Challis National Forest 
                    Lemhi County, Idaho
desc: The 4A 14'x14' cab on Sagebrush Lookout on the Salmon-Challis National Forest dates to 1926. Last staffed in 2000, it is badly in need of adoption and restoration.

name: Salmon Mountain Lookout
loc:
Bitterroot National Forest 
                    Idaho County, Idaho
desc: The honor of NHLR listing #800 goes to Salmon Mountain Lookout on the Bitterroot National Forest. First developed as a tent camp with alidade, in 1938, it was replaced with a log L-3 cupola with windows around the first floor. This classic 1936 model L-4 ground house with catwalk was built in 1949 and is staffed by volunteers. Salmon Mountain Lookout is the only L-4 ground cab remaining in the area. Located in the Frank Church River of No Return Wilderness, less than a mile south of the Magruder Corridor and the Montana Road, Salmon Mountain also looks into the Selway Bitterroot Wilderness to the north of the corridor. In recent years, it has been staffed by a volunteer group.

name: Scott Mountain Lookout
loc:
Boise National Forest 
                    Boise County, Idaho
desc: An L-4 cab built in 1934 on an unusual 28'x28' stone foundation/catwalk, Scott Mountain Lookout remains in active service. It replaced a 12'x12' log cabin built in 1920 on the Boise National forest.

name: Scurvy Mountain Lookout
loc:
Clearwater National Forest 
                    Clearwater County, Idaho
desc: The first lookout on Scurvy Mountain on the Clearwater National Forest was a platform in 1917 with a cabin added in 1935. The present L-4 cab (without outriggers) was built in 1952 and staffed until 1978 when placed on emergency status. The structure has been gradually restored by local volunteers over a 10 year period.

name: Shafer Butte Lookout
loc:
Boise National Forest 
                    Boise County, Idaho
desc:
Up in the hills north of Boise is a most unusual lookout on top of a lookout. First established in 1926 by the Southern Idaho Timber Protective Association with a two-story cabin, 
 Shafer Butte Lookout was replaced in 1958 when the Boise National Forest constructed a 14' x 14' R-6 flattop cab on a 10' concrete block base. The ground floor was used for living quarters many years ago, and later was used as a radio and storage room. The second floor then became living quarters. As the radio towers expanded, the third floor was used for the alidade and observation. 
 In the late 80s or 90s, the Bogus Basin ski patrol began to occupy the second floor. The lookout is now used in emergencies.

name: Sheep Hill Lookout
loc:
Nez Perce National Forest 
                    Idaho County, Idaho
desc: Sheep Hill Lookout lies deep within the Frank Church River of No Return Wilderness. From the summit once can see portions of the Payette and Bitterroot National Forests, as well as the Nez Perce. The current R-6 flattop on a 7’ concrete base was built in 1960, replacing a log cupola cabin dating to 1928. It remains in active service.

name: Sheepeater Lookout
loc:
Payette National Forest 
                    Idaho County, Idaho
desc: One of the oldest lookouts still in full-time use within the Frank Church River of No Return Wilderness on the Payette National Forest in Idaho, it is also among the most remote. Sheepeater Lookout is named for a small tribe of Indians who earlier lived in the region. The current CL-100 14’x14' flat roof cab with catwalk on a 6' stone base and storage room was erected in 1976, replacing a L-4 ground house built in 1957 which itself replaced a log structure dating to the 1920s. In addition to fire detection, the lookout is an important recreation and communications contact point in the wilderness.

name: Shissler Peak Lookout
loc:
Nez Perce National Forest 
                    Idaho County, Idaho
desc: The Nez Perce National Forest built Shissler Peak Lookout in 1933. It was an L-4 cab on a pole tower. In l953 the current 1936 model L-4 with catwalk was constructed on a 10’ treated timber tower. Shissler Peak sits above the confluence of Moose Creek and the Selway River within the Selway-Bitterroot Wilderness Area in the Nez Perce National Forest. Shissler is regularly staffed for fire detection.

name: Short Creek Lookout
loc:
Salmon-Challis National Forest 
                    Valley County, Idaho
desc: An orphan wilderness lookout on the Salmon National Forest, Short Creek is an L-4 cab ground house built in 1934 and abandoned in the 1950s. It is in need of a friend.

name: Shorty Peak Lookout
loc:
Idaho Panhandle National Forests 
                    Boundary County, Idaho
desc: Accessible via a 2 ½ mile trail, the first lookout on Shorty Peak on the Kaniksu National Forest was a cupola cabin built in 1927. In 1964 the present 14’x14’ R-6 flattop with catwalk on a 8’ concrete base was constructed. It is now in the recreation rental system.

name: Silver Creek Lookout
loc:
Boise National Forest 
                    Valley County, Idaho
desc: This L-4 cab sits atop a 24'x24' concrete base. It was built in 1936 and is staffed during the summer.

name: Slate Point Lookout
loc:
Nez Perce National Forest 
                    Idaho County, Idaho
desc: The first Slate Point Lookout was a 75’ pole tower with 7’x7’ cab and ground quarters built in 1931. The Nez Perce National Forest replaced it with an L-4 cab on a 41’ tower in 1948, which in turn was replaced by this R-6 flattop cab with catwalk on a 41’ timber tower in 1979. Nearby Slate Creek was named after early miners who found no placer gravel in the stream, only slate. Slate Point Lookout has been staffed in most recent years.

name: Sleeping Deer Mountain Lookout
loc:
Salmon Challis National Forest 
                    Custer County, Idaho
desc: Sleeping Deer Mountain lookout is on the northern section of the Challis National Forest, close to where the Boise, Payette, and Salmon National Forests join. The hip roof L-4 groundhouse with catwalk was built in 1935 and last staffed in 1997 and is now on emergency status.

name: Sloans Point Lookout
loc:
Payette National Forest 
                    Valley County, Idaho
desc: When it was constructed in 1933, the materials for Sloans Point Lookout on the Payette National Forest were hauled in by wagon. The 72’ Aermotor tower with 7’x7’ metal cab was staffed into the 1970s. The log cabin residence was removed in 1994 and in 2000 volunteers dismantled the tower and reconstructed the cab and 10’ of the tower at the Central Idaho Historical Museum in McCall.

name: Snow Peak Lookout
loc:
St. Joe National Forest 
                    Shoshone County, Idaho
desc: This R-6 cab lookout was built in 1963.

name: Sourdough Peak Lookout
loc:
Nez Perce National Forest 
                    Idaho County, Idaho
desc: Constructed in 1927 using the "Nez Perce Log Lookout House Plan,” Sourdough Peak Lookout is unique. Although the blueprints called for a 16’ x 14’ structure, the builder modified it to 15’x 15’ and added windows all around. In 1994 and 1995 the Nez Perce National Forest conducted a complete restoration as a Passport in Time Project using skilled volunteers and Forest Service personnel.

name: Spades Mountain Lookout
loc:
Idaho Panhandle National Forests 
                    Kootenai County, Idaho
desc:
This lookout began in 1923 as a camp lookout. A 50' pole tower with 7x7' cab was built in 1926, with a log cabin added for living quarters in 1928. In 1941, a 54' steel tower was built, with an L-4 cab added for living quarters in the 1940s. That steel tower was moved to Long Mountain Lookout in 1963, replaced by the present 67' treated timber tower with R-6 flat cab, which has not been staffed since the 1970s.
 

 
The tower was removed in July 2015. The ground house remains.

name: Spot Mountain Lookout
loc:
Bitterroot National Forest 
                    Idaho County, Idaho
desc: In 1922 the Bitterroot National Forest built the first Spot Mountain Lookout, a two story log cabin with windows on all sides. In 1934 it was replaced by an L-4 on a 10’ tower. The current R-6 flattop with catwalk on a 10’ concrete base was built in 1972. Spot Mountain Lookout sits in the Selway Bitterroot Wilderness Area overlooking the Selway River. Located in the Idaho portion of the Bitterroot National Forest, management of the lookout has at times switched back and forth between the Bitterroot and Nez Perce forests, but Spot Mountain is currently managed by the Bitterroot and is staffed as funding allows.

name: Spyglass Lookout
loc:
Coeur D'Alene National Forest 
                    Shoshone County, Idaho
desc: Started in 1922 with a 20' platform tower, log cabin and barn, a 50' pole tower with 7'x7' cab replaced the first tower in 1930. In 1943, a gable roof L-4 cab was moved from another site for living quarters on the ground, later remodeled for storage, and is still on the summit. The present standard 53' CT-2 treated timber tower with standard 1936-model L-4 cab, built in 1950, was last staffed in 1978. Spyglass is unique in that it still has two generations of lookout structures, the 53' tower with L-4 cab, and the L-4 ground house. At the time of the 1973 consolidation in North Idaho, Spyglass was one of two Magee Ranger District Lookouts.

name: Square Mountain Lookout
loc:
Nez Perce National Forest 
                    Idaho County, Idaho
desc: There were only a few of the famed “Nez Perce L-5” log cabin lookouts built, and Square Mountain is one of the best of the last on the Nez Perce National Forest. Built in 1931 and in service until the 1970s, the cabin is being carefully restored by the regional Historic Preservation Team and a Pass Passport In Time project with lightning protection materials from the Idaho/Montana FFLA chapter.

name: Stein Mountain Lookout
loc:
Salmon-Challis National Forest 
                    Lemhi County, Idaho
desc: Built in 1958 on the Salmon National Forest, the Stein Mountain Lookout is a 15'x15' R-6 cab with catwalk and a unique carport. It replaced a log cabin lookout built in 1917.

name: Stoddard Creek Lookout
loc:
Salmon-Challis National Forest 
                    Idaho County, Idaho
desc: Built in 1934, this lookout was occupied from about 1941 through the mid-1970s.

name: Stormy Peak Lookout
loc:
Salmon-Challis National Forest 
                    Lemhi County, Idaho
desc:
A modified L-4 cab on a one-story log base, Stormy Peak Lookout was built on the Salmon-Challis National Forest in 1928 replacing a tent camp activated in 1920. 
 Stormy Peak was reported lost in the Moose Fire on July 25, 2022.

name: Sundance Lookout
loc: Bonner County, Idaho
desc: Sundance Lookout first went into service as a tent camp with an alidade on the rock pile in 1928. Seven years later the first permanent structure, an L-4 hip-roofed cab on a 20’ log tower in 1935. That lookout somehow survived the firestorm of the Sundance fire in 1967, but the Idaho Department of Lands replaced it in 1981 with an R-6 flattop cab with catwalk on a 20’ timber tower. A volunteer program is currently used to staff Sundance Lookout.

name: Sunset Mountain Lookout
loc:
Boise National Forest 
                    Boise County, Idaho
desc: Sunset Mountain Lookout on the Boise National Forest was originally a R-5 cab on a 10' concrete base built in 1930. This R-6 cab with catwalk was constructed on the same base in 1958.

name: Surveyors Ridge Lookout
loc:
Idaho Panhandle National Forest 
                    Shoshone County, Idaho
desc: The first lookout on Surveyor’s Ridge on the St. Joe National Forest was a gabled L-4 on a 20’ pole tower built in 1931. In 1964 it was replaced by the current R-6 15’ x 15’ flattop with catwalk on a 20’ timber tower. In active service until recent years the lookout -- which overlooks the Mallard-Larkins Pioneer Area -- has been added to the cabin rental program.

name: Twin Peaks Lookout
loc:
Challis National Forest 
                    Custer County, Idaho
desc: This 15'x15' R-6 lookout sites on a 10-foot concrete base. It was built in 1964 to replace a 1932 L-4 lookout.

name: Ulysses Mountain Lookout
loc:
Salmon-Challis National Forest 
                    Lemhi County, Idaho
desc: One of the relatively few 7'x7' cabs on a steel tower in Idaho, Ulysses Mountain Lookout and log cabin living quarters were built in 1928 on the Salmon-Challis National Forest

name: Walde Mountain Lookout
loc:
Clearwater National Forest 
                    Idaho County, Idaho
desc: One of a few 7’x7’ fire towers on the Clearwater National Forest, Walde Mountain Lookout has a 100’ metal tower built in 1939. A log cabin ground house was added in 1941. The lookout is staffed.

name: Weitas Butte Lookout
loc:
Clearwater National Forest 
                    Idaho County, Idaho
desc:
Weitas Butte Lookout (originally named Wet Ass) is a 14’x14’ L-4 cab with catwalk on a 53’ timber tower built on the Clearwater National Forest in 1953, replacing an L-4 on a 30’ pole tower dating to 1931.
 

 
In 1983 it became one of the first lookouts placed in the rental system. While not currently available for rent, it is expected to return to the rental system in 2015.

name: Whitehawk Lookout
loc:
Boise National Forest 
                    Valley County, Idaho
desc: An L-4 groundhouse with catwalk, Whitehawk Lookout remains active. It was built in 1933 on the Boise National Forest.

name: Wild Horse Lookout
loc:
Challis National Forest 
                    Custer County, Idaho
desc: This L-4 ground cab was built in 1935 and abandoned in 1946. It was subsequently restored in the 1970s.

name: South Mountain Lookout
loc:
Boise District - Bureau of Land Management 
                    Owyhee County, Idaho
admin: Department of the Interior - Bureau of Land Management
desc: South Mountain first hosted a lookout cabin in 1933. The cabin was replaced by the current structure in 1964. South Mountain is generally staffed during the fire season.

name: Mount Harrison Lookout
loc:
Sawtooth National Forest 
                    Cassia County, Idaho
admin: US Forest Service - Sawtooth National Forest
desc:
A lookout was originally constructed on Mount Harrison in 1942. The building was replaced with the current structure in 1977. 
 Mount Harrison has a commanding view of lands in Southern Idaho, northern Nevada and Utah. The lookout is generally staffed during fire season and visitors are welcome on weekends.

name: Sedgewick Peak Lookout
loc: Bannock County, Idaho
desc:
Sedgewick Peak was constructed for the Idaho Department of Lands in an extended building period from 1973-77. 
 The building now houses communications equipment.

name: Notch Butte Lookout
loc:
Twin Falls District - Bureau of Land Management 
                    Lincoln County, Idaho
admin: Department of the Interior - Bureau of Land Management
desc:
Notch Butte was constructed in 1941, a USFS Region 1 Plan ground cabin. 
 The site was used into the 2000's before being converted to a communications facility.

name: Squaw Butte Lookout
loc:
Boise District - Bureau of Land Management 
                    Gem County, Idaho
admin: Department of the Interior - Bureau of Land Management
desc:
Squaw Butte - South has hosted a lookout since 1933. Structures were replaced in 1938, 1953 and finally 1981 with the current 2 story building. 
 Squaw Butte is generally staffed during fire season.

name: Danskin Peak Lookout
loc:
Boise National Forest 
                    Elmore County, Idaho
admin: US Forest Service - Boise National Forest
desc:
Danskin Peak, a wood frame 16x16 cabin on a stone first story was built in 1940. 
 The lookout is generally staffed during the fire season.

name: Trinity Lookout
loc:
Boise National Forest 
                    Elmore County, Idaho
admin: US Forest Service - Boise National Forest
desc:
Trinity Mountain has hosted a lookout since 1922. A 12x12 stone cabin first, later replaced by an L-4 cabin on a 10 foot concrete block tower. 
 Trinity Lookout is generally staffed during the fire season.

name: Swanholm Peak Lookout
loc:
Boise National Forest 
                    Elmore County, Idaho
admin: US Forest Service - Boise National Forest
desc:
Swanholm Peak has been a fire detection site since 1921. A log, ground cabin was built in 1922. It was replaced by the current Region 1 Plan cabin on a 10 foot concrete block tower in 1954. 
 The forest no longer staffs Swanholm Peak but it is kept in shape ready for emergency duty if needed.

name: Hawley Mountain Lookout
loc:
Boise National Forest 
                    Boise County, Idaho
admin: US Forest Service - Boise National Forest
desc: Hawley Mountain was constructed in 1935, an R1/L-4 cabin on an enclosed 8 foot tower.

name: Jackson Peak Lookout
loc:
Boise National Forest 
                    Boise County, Idaho
admin: US Forest Service - Boise National Forest
desc:
The first lookout was constructed on Jackson Peak in 1927. Similar to a California Plan 4A.   
 The current 2 story structure was constructed in 1979 and continues to be staffed each fire season.

name: Thorn Creek Butte Lookout
loc:
Boise National Forest 
                    Boise County, Idaho
admin: US Forest Service - Boise National Forest
desc:
Thorn Creek Butte was constructed in 1933. A classic L-4 cabin atop a 10 foot enclosed tower. 
 The lookout is available for emergencies.

name: Bald Mountain Lookout
loc:
Sawtooth National Forest 
                    Blaine County, Idaho
admin: US Forest Service - Sawtooth National Forest
desc:
Bald Mountain has hosted a lookout structure since 1921. The second structure was an L-4 cabin on a stone base built in 1937. The current building was constructed in 1958. 
 Staffing was discontinued in the mid-1990's

name: Granite Mountain Lookout
loc:
Payette National Forest 
                    Adams County, Idaho
admin: US Forest Service - Payette National Forest
desc:
Granite Mountain began as a camp in 1913, a 10' pole tower with 12x12' cab was built in 1916. 
 The present 20' treated timber L-4 tower, constructed in 1955, is staffed every fire season.

name: Horse Mountain Lookout
loc:
Payette National Forest 
                    Adams County, Idaho
admin: US Forest Service - Payette National Forest
desc: The lookout at Horse Mountain was constructed in 1935. An R1/L-4 cabin on a 30 foot open timber tower.

name: Jackley Mountain Lookout
loc:
Payette National Forest 
                    Adams County, Idaho
admin: US Forest Service - Payette National Forest
desc: Jackley Mountain, an R1/L-4 ground cabin was constructed in 1932 and was no longer staffed after 1948.

name: Lick Creek Point Lookout
loc:
Payette National Forest 
                    Adams County, Idaho
admin: US Forest Service - Payette National Forest
desc:
Lick Creek Point Lookout was established in 1932 with an R1/L-4 cabin on an enclosed timber tower. The current structure, an R-6 flat cab was constructed in 1978. 
 Lick Creek Point is generally staffed during the fire season.

name: Pollock Mountain Lookout
loc:
Payette National Forest 
                    Adams County, Idaho
admin: US Forest Service - Payette National Forest
desc:
Pollock Mountain Lookout was constructed in 1930, a 14'x14' ground cabin. 
 The lookout is generally staffed during fire season.

name: Smith Mountain Lookout
loc:
Payette National Forest 
                    Adams County, Idaho
admin: US Forest Service - Payette National Forest
desc:
Smith Mountain has been used as a lookout site since 1908, a cupola cabin was constructed in 1920 and was replaced by an R1/L-4 cabin in 1932 
 The current Smith Mountain Lookout was constructed in 1963, an R-6 Flat Top.

name: Iron Mountain Lookout
loc:
Sawtooth National Forest 
                    Camas County, Idaho
admin: US Forest Service - Sawtooth National Forest
desc:
A lookout cabin was built atop Iron Mountain in 1922, a California Region 5 Plan 4A design.  
 The structure was replaced in 1961 with the current R-6 Flat Top on an enclosed tower.

name: Mount Greylock Lookout
loc:
Salmon-Challis National Forest 
                    Custer County, Idaho
admin: US Forest Service - Salmon-Challis National Forest
desc:
Mount Greylock Lookout was constructed in 1935, a standard R1/L-4 ground cabin with a Forest design catwalk. 
 The lookout was used, sometimes as a training site during the CCC era and was abandoned in 1939 or 40. After more than 80 years from it's last use, it still stands.

name: Jureano Mountain Lookout
loc:
Salmon-Challis National Forest 
                    Lemhi County, Idaho
admin: US Forest Service - Salmon-Challis National Forest
desc:
Jureano Mountain was constructed in 1935, a 7x7 observation cabin on a 60 foot open steel tower. 
 The lookout was last staffed in the 1950's.

name: Long Tom Lookout
loc:
Salmon-Challis National Forest 
                    Lemhi County, Idaho
admin: US Forest Service - Salmon-Challis National Forest
desc:
The current structure is the fourth on Long Tom Mountain. A 2 story log cabin was constructed in 1923, replaced in 1933 and again in the 40's with a R1/L-4 cabin on a log crib. 
 Today's lookout was built in 1977 and is generally staffed during the fire season.

name: Sal Mountain Lookout
loc:
Salmon-Challis National Forest 
                    Lemhi County, Idaho
admin: US Forest Service - Salmon-Challis National Forest
desc:
Sal Mountain is a 10x10 wood frame ground cabin completed in 1926. 
 The lookout has not been staffed since the 1940's and continues to stand.

name: Sheephorn Mountain Lookout
loc:
Salmon-Challis National Forest 
                    Lemhi County, Idaho
admin: US Forest Service - Salmon-Challis National Forest
desc: Sheephorn Mountain has hosted a lookout since 1933. The first was a 9x9 cabin, replaced in 1965 with a Region 6 Plan Flat Cab.

name: Taylor Mountain Lookout
loc:
Salmon-Challis National Forest 
                    Lemhi County, Idaho
admin: US Forest Service - Salmon-Challis National Forest
desc:
Taylor Mountain was first identified as a lookout site in the 1920's. A 6x6 cabin and camp were constructed. The structure was replaced in 1930 with a 10x10 log crib ground cabin. 
 The site was abandoned in 1956. The structure remains standing.

name: Big Baldy Lookout
loc:
Boise National Forest 
                    Valley County, Idaho
admin: US Forest Service - Boise National Forest
desc:
A log cabin with cupola structure was completed at Big Baldy in 1924. A Region 6 Plan Flat Top cabin on an enclosed tower replaced the original building in 1959. 
 Big Baldy is located within the Frank Church River of No Return Wilderness.

name: Brundage Lookout
loc:
Payette National Forest 
                    Valley County, Idaho
desc:
Brundage Lookout began as with a log cabin camp in 1914. A two story 18x18 log structure was built in 1919 and replaced with a 20x20 log lookout in 1929. 
 The current structure was constructed in 1982, a 2 story concrete and wood flat top design on a rubble base. 
 The area is very popular with hikers in the Summer and skiers at the Brundage Resort in the Winter. 
 The lookout is staffed every fire season by the Southern Idaho Timber Protective Association.

name: Gold Fork Lookout
loc:
Boise National Forest 
                    Valley County, Idaho
admin: US Forest Service - Boise National Forest
desc:
Gold Fork Lookout was originally located on a precarious rock ledge with a long staircase to an open platform. The site began operation in circa 1918-20. 
 A new lookout, an R1/L-4 cabin on a 10 foot 20x20 concrete base was built 2 miles from the original location in 1933.  
 The lookout's use was eventually discontinued and the cabin was relocated to the Crawford Forest Work Center northeast of Cascade in 1988.

name: Miners Peak Lookout
loc:
Payette National Forest 
                    Valley County, Idaho
admin: US Forest Service - Payette National Forest
desc:
A gable roof R1/L-4 cabin was relocated from Teapot Dome in 1948 to establish the lookout site at Miners Peak. 
 A new 2 story, wood frame lookout was constructed in 1986. 
 The lookout is generally staffed during fire season.

name: Morehead Mountain Lookout
loc:
Boise National Forest 
                    Valley County, Idaho
desc:
Morehead Mountain Lookout was originally constructed in 1933 and destroyed that year by a lightning strike. The R1/L-4 ground cabin was rebuilt in 1934. 
 The lookout was refurbished by a Treasure Valley Back Country Horsemen volunteer crew in 2015, including the removal on a non-original catwalk. 
 The lookout is located within the Frank Church River of No Return Wilderness. 
 Morehead Mountain was reported destroyed in the Boundary Fire on September 9, 2021.

name: No Business Lookout
loc:
Payette National Forest 
                    Valley County, Idaho
desc:
No Business Mountain has been a fire detection site since the 1920's. First as a camp then in 1937 a 2 story, 20x20 log structure was built. This building was replaced with a duplicate design in 1963. 
 No Business Lookout is staffed during the fire season and welcomes visitors.

name: Norton Ridge Lookout
loc:
Boise National Forest 
                    Valley County, Idaho
admin: US Forest Service - Boise National Forest
desc:
The Norton Ridge Lookout was constructed by the Civilian Conservation Corps in 1933 and is located within the boundaries of the Frank Church River of No Return Wilderness Area.   
  It is a ground mounted L-4 standard design of the 1930’s and is eligible to be listed on the National Register of Historic Places.  
  The Treasure Valley Back Country Horsemen replaced the roof and did some paint work on the lookout in 2014.

name: Pilot Peak Lookout
loc:
Payette National Forest 
                    Valley County, Idaho
admin: US Forest Service - Payette National Forest
desc:
Pilot Peak Lookout was first established in 1919 with a 12x12 log ground cabin. 
 A new structure, an R1/L-4 plan on a 10 foot block, enclosed tower was built in 1954. 
 Pilot Peak is generally staffed during the fire season.

name: Shellrock Peak Lookout
loc:
Payette National Forest 
                    Valley County, Idaho
admin: US Forest Service - Payette National Forest
desc: Shellrock Peak Lookout, an R1/L-4 Plan ground cabin was built in 1935. The lookout was no longer staffed after 1950 but still stands today.

name: Split Creek Point Lookout
loc:
Central Idaho Historical Museum 
                    Valley County, Idaho
desc:
Split Creek Point Lookout and residence cabin were constructed in 1933. The lookout structure was an Aermotor 7x7 observation cabin atop a 72 foot X-Brace open steel tower. 
 The lookout tower was disassembled in 2008 with the residence cabin remaining at the original site.  
 The lookout cab was relocated to the Central Idaho Historical Museum in McCall, Idaho and may be toured by visitors.

name: Thunderbolt Mountain Lookout
loc:
Boise National Forest 
                    Valley County, Idaho
admin: US Forest Service - Boise National Forest
desc:
Thunderbolt Mountain has hosted a lookout point since 1917. First a camp, then in 1933 a D-6 Plan cupola structure was built. 
 The current lookout is a Region 6 Plan Flat Cab built in 1962 or 1965. 
 Thunderbolt Mountain is generally staffed during the fire season.

name: Tripod Peak Lookout
loc:
Boise National Forest 
                    Valley County, Idaho
desc:
Tripod Peak first hosted a lookout in 1921. A California Region 5 Plan 4A cabin was constructed on a 6 foot open timber tower. This structure was replace by an R1/L-4 cabin cabin on a short open, timber tower. A concrete base was added in 1950. 
 The current Region 6 Plan Flat Cab was constructed in 1977.  
 The lookout is staffed during the fire season by the Southern Idaho Timber Protection Association.

name: Williams Peak Lookout
loc:
Payette National Forest 
                    Valley County, Idaho
desc:
Williams Peak Lookout was constructed in 1932, an R1/L-4 ground cabin. 
 The lookout is generally staffed each fire season.

name: Sturgill Peak Lookout
loc:
Payette National Forest 
                    Washington County, Idaho
admin: US Forest Service - Payette National Forest
desc:
Sturgill Peak is a Region1/L-4 cabin design on a short, stone rubble tower. 
 Built in 1932, it continues to be staffed for fire detection.

name: Black Butte Lookout
loc:
Nez Perce National Forest 
                    Idaho County, Idaho
admin: US Forest Service - Nez Perce National Forest
desc:
Black Butte has hosted a fire detection site since 1925. The first permanent structure was built in 1928. 
 The current lookout was built in 1970, an USFS Region 6 Flat Top design on an 8 foot block tower.

name: Hershey Point Lookout
loc:
Payette National Forest 
                    Idaho County, Idaho
admin: US Forest Service - Payette National Forest
desc:
Hershey Point Lookout first construction was a Region 1/L-4 design ground cabin built circa 1932. 
 A new structure was built in 1966, a Region 6 Flat Top cabin design on a 10 foot block tower.

name: War Eagle Lookout
loc:
Payette National Forest 
                    Idaho County, Idaho
admin: US Forest Service - Payette National Forest
desc:
The original War Eagle Lookout was a 10 foot log crib tower with a Region 1/L-4 cabin atop. 
 In 1961 a new structure was built, a Region 6 Flat Top design on a 10 foot block tower. 
 War Eagle is generally staffed during the fire season.

name: Black Mountain Lookout
loc:
Idaho Panhandle National Forests 
                    Boundary County, Idaho
desc:
Black Mountain's first lookout was constructed in 1921, a Region 5 Plan 4A cabin on a short open timber tower. It was replace in 1935 with an Region 1/L-4 cabin on a 40 foot pole tower. 
 The current structure, a Region 6 Flat Top on a 53 foot open timber tower, was constructed in 1963 at Faset Peak and moved to Black Mountain in 1975. 
 The lookout survived vandal damage to it's tower legs and was moved to a new location 1/2 mile ENE of the original site in 2019 with a plan to add it to the recreational rental program.

name: West Fork Lookout
loc:
Idaho Panhandle National Forests 
                    Boundary County, Idaho
admin: US Forest Service - Idaho Panhandle National Forests
desc:
West Fork Lookout, an Aermotor 7x7 cabin atop a 35 foot steel, X-Brace tower was constructed in 1934 along with a frame residence cabin. 
 Only the tower remains, not having been staffed since the 1950's.

name: St. Joe Baldy Lookout
loc:
Idaho Panhandle National Forests 
                    Benewah County, Idaho
admin: US Forest Service/Idaho Department of Lands
desc:
St. Joe Baldy was constructed in 1954 replacing an earlier lookout site about a mile away. 
 A Region 1/L-4 cabin was placed atop a 10 foot block tower. 
 The lookout has not been staffed since the 1980's. The catwalk, shutters and stairs have been removed. The structure is now used as a communications vault.

name: Eagle Point Lookout
loc:
Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forests 
                    Clearwater County, Idaho
admin: US Forest Service - Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forests
desc:
The current Region 6 Flat Top cabin sits atop a 41 foot open timber tower and was constructed in 1973. 
 The first structure, a two story log cabin was built in 1935 and was replaced by a Region 1/L-4 cabin on a 41 foot open timber tower. 
 The lookout is still occasionally staffed during emergencies.

name: Wallow Mountain Lookout
loc:
Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forests 
                    Clearwater County, Idaho
admin: US Forest Service - Nez Perce-Clearwater National Forests
desc:
Wallow Mountain Lookout was constructed in 1968, a Region 6 Flat Top cabin on a 10 foot open timber tower. 
 The first structure was completed in the 1920's, a D-6 Cupola cabin. A new Region 1/L-4 cabin atop a log crib was built in 1932 before being replaced by the current structure.

name: Balancing Rock Lookout
loc:
Nez Perce - Clearwater National Forests 
                    Clearwater County, Idaho
admin: US Forest Service - Nez Perce - Clearwater National Forests
desc:
This L-6 design cabin was built in 1933 and is the only known surviving structure of the type in Idaho. 
 The L-6 was an 8x8 wood frame, observation only cabin frequently used as a secondary, emergency or patrol point site. 
 A restoration was undertaken during 2013 and 2014.

name: Poirier Tree Farm Lookout
loc:
Private Tree Farm 
                    Bonner County, Idaho
desc:
The lookout is a 2 story, 14x14 design built on a private tree farm in the 1930's. 
 The structure is in poor shape as of 2017 and is in danger of collapse.

name: Russell Mountain Lookout
loc:
Idaho Panhandle National Forests 
                    Boundary County, Idaho
desc:
A camp with an alidade was established in 1927, a cabin built in the 1930's. 
 The site was not staffed after 1967. The tower was removed sometime after that point, although the lookout cabin was left.

name: Saddle Mountain Lookout
loc:
Idaho Panhandle National Forests 
                    Boundary County, Idaho
admin: US Forest Service - Idaho Panhandle National Forests
desc:
Saddle Mountain Lookout was constructed in 1935, a 7x7 Aermotor observation only  cabin on a 40 foot X-Brace steel tower. A residence cabin was also provided. 
 The lookout site has not been staffed since the late 1960's.

name: Mid-cottonwood Point Lookout
loc:
Salmon-Challis National Forest, Challis portion 
                    Custer County, Idaho
desc: Originally, a standard L-4 cabin was built here in 1934 by the U.S. Forest Service. It was abandoned in 1946 and no longer serves as an active fire tower.

name: Aeneas Lookout
loc:
Washington Dept. of Natural Resources - Northeast Division 
                    Okanogan County, Washington
desc:
The first Aeneas Lookout located on this eastern Washington mountain top was a one room log cabin built in 1920 by the U.S. Forest Service. The site has been continuously staffed by observers since then--including Ray Kresek, the authority on lookouts in the Pacific Northwest. 
 During that time there have been four different structures. The present 40’ wooden tower with a 14’x 14’ flattop live-in cab with catwalk was built by the Washington Dept. of Natural Resources in 1980. 
 Aeneas was the longest continually staffed lookout in Washington at 104 seasons. The lookout was last staffed in 2020.

name: Alpine Lookout
loc:
Wenatchee National Forest 
                    Chelan County, Washington
desc: Still the domain of mountain goats and sweeping vistas of the Washington Cascade Range, the site of the aptly named Alpine Lookout on the Wenatchee National Forest was first used for fire detection in 1920 when an outdoor alidade, phone, and tent were set up. In 1936 a L-4 groundhouse was constructed with an oversize stone base. The structure was replaced in 1975 with a 15’x 15’ standard R-6 flattop cab which remains in active service today and is only accessible by trail.

name: Big Butte Lookout
loc:
Umatilla National Forest 
                    Asotin County, Washington
desc: Located on the Umatilla National Forest in southeastern Washington just north of the Oregon state line, Big Butte Lookout has been in standby status for a number of years. First established in 1938 with a L-6 cab on a 73' pole tower, it was replaced by the even higher 82' treated timber tower with L-4 cab and catwalk in 1950.

name: Buck Mountain Lookout
loc: Okanogan County, Washington
desc: Buck Mountain Lookout was developed in 1919 by the state as a crow's nest and log cabin. In 1934 a 20' pole L-4 tower was built, and it was replaced in 1961 with the present 14' x 14' flat-gable Washington Department of Natural Resources live-in cab with catwalk on a 20' timber tower. It is maintained by the DNR for emergency use.

name: Burley Mountain Lookout
loc:
Gifford Pinchot National Forest 
                    Lewis County, Washington
desc: Located in the middle of a triangle between Mt. Ranier, Mt. St. Helens and Mt. Adams, Burley Mountain Lookout offers a spectacular view of the southern Cascade Mountains. The 14' x 14' ground house with no catwalk is a classic L-4 built in 1934.

name: Cleman Mountain Lookout
loc:
Wenatchee National Forest 
                    Yakima County, Washington
desc:
Overlooking the remote Oak Creek Wildlife Area in eastern Washington, Cleman Mountain Lookout was established by the Division of Forestry after the war in 1946 with a cabin. An L-4 cab was built on the site in 1954. The present 14' x 14' DNR flat-gable live-in cab on a 40' timber tower was built in 1968 and last staffed by the Wenatchee National Forest in 1998. 
  Cleman Mountain Lookout was damaged in a storm in 2006 and destroyed in 2007.

name: Columbia Mountain Lookout
loc:
Colville National Forest 
                    Ferry County, Washington
desc:
In 1914 the U.S. Forest Service constructed the Columbia Mountain Lookout on the Colville National Forest.  It was designed by the second supervisor of the forest, CC Reed. It is characterized by a unique 12’x12’ log cabin of hand hewn timbers with interlocking tapered walls and corner posts that supported a 15’ high platform overhead.   The cabin was converted to a storage shed when in 1928 a 16’ pole tower lookout with wooden cab was constructed and remained in service until the mid-1950s. It was burned in the 1960s.  The original log cabin – sans platform -- remains.  In 1993 initial restoration work on the aging cabin was performed by the Washington Chapter of the Forest Fire Lookout Association led by Ray Kresek.
 

 
During the summers of 2009 and 2010, Passport In Time volunteers and Forest Service employees led by forest archaeologist Stuart Chilvers restored the lookout.  New hand hewn squared wall logs, floor and new framework hand peeled for the roof replace rotted sections.  Then finished with new shake roofing.     As much as possible of the original lookout was reused, including old magazines used as chinking.  It is hoped that this authentic restoration will allow the lookout to last another 95 years.

name: Copper Mountain Lookout
loc:
North Cascades National Park 
                    Whatcom County, Washington
desc: Surrounded by spectacular scenery of upended spires and broken glaciers, Copper Mountain Lookout, a L-4 ground cabin without catwalk, was built on Copper Mountain by the U.S. Forest Service in 1932. Located on the Mount Baker National Forest and accessible only by a 10 mile trail, it was staffed each summer as a lookout and a wilderness guard station. With the creation of North Cascades National Park in 1968, the entire area was transferred to the National Park Service. It has continued to be staffed each summer by the NPS.

name: Desolation Peak Lookout
loc:
North Cascades National Park 
                    Whatcom County, Washington
desc: Desolation Peak Lookout was also established by the Forest Service on the Mount Baker National Forest and later transferred to the North Cascades National Park. The 14' x 14' L-4 ground house without catwalk was built in 1933 and remains active under the NPS. Accessible by trail 23 miles from the nearest road, or 13 miles up Ross Lake and then 7 miles of trail, it is one of the most remote active lookouts in the U.S.

name: Dodger Point Lookout
loc:
Olympic National Park 
                    Challam County, Washington
desc:
This lookout features a 14'x14' L-4 cab and was built by the US Forest Service in 1933. It was also used as an Aircraft Warning Service station. It was placed on the National Register of Historic Places on July 13, 2007. Along with the Pyramid Peak Lookout, they are the last two lookouts still standing in the Olympic National Park.
