The last active station overlooking the Willamette Valley, Green Peter Lookout first went into service as a cabin in 1916, which was soon replaced with a cupola lookout in 1920. In 1970 the Linn Forest Protection Ass’n. and the Oregon Dept. of Forestry moved the present L-4 live-in cab to the site from Jordan where it was originally constructed in 1949.
 

 
Additional information courtesy of Jim Basting: "In 2000 we had a new tin roof put on which changed the roof line. Also in 2004 the lookout was rebuilt. It was torn down to the stud walls and all dry rot was removed and replaced with new material. New windows, door, siding, shutters, trim, catwalk and guard rail were all replaced. It is holding up well and still looks brand new."; "With the advent of “smoke detection” cameras we no longer man Green Peter Lookout. There is a camera mounted on top of a 120 foot tall radio tower adjacent to GPLO which makes a 360 degree rotation every six minutes and can be controlled manually if a fire is spotted. It is very interesting technology and seems to work fairly well. We also have a “smoke detection” camera on Cougar Rock ( A USFS repeater site) about 13 miles to the East of Green Peter that covers the Cascade Mountain portion Sweet Home Unit of the South Cascade District. This camera covers a portion of what the USFS Iron Mountain Lookout used to see."

name: Green Ridge Lookout
loc:
Deschutes National Forest 
                    Deschutes County, Oregon
desc: Green Ridge Lookout is a “side hill” site -- as compared to a mountaintop -- looking into the Metolious River drainage and Mt. Jefferson within the Deschutes National Forest in Oregon’s central Cascades. The first lookout was a Standard L-5 10x10 finished in 1934 and was classified as an emergency station. The current 15’ x 15’ R-6 flattop with catwalk on a 21’ timber tower was constructed in 1961 and is regularly staffed by volunteers.

name: Halls Point Lookout
loc:
Rogue River National Forest 
                    Jackson County, Oregon
desc: Prior to the construction of the current R-6, this point was primarily a secondary site of Whetstone Point. It was on Whetstone (in early days called Old Baldy or Bald Mountain) that the crows nest was located in a 80 foot tree in 1914. In 1920 a standard D-6 cupola was built, in 1934 the cupola was elevated onto a ten foot tower. In 1951 the State erected the 40 foot tower at the south end of the ridge (White Point). Whetstone Point being located at the mid point of the ridge was not very effective for the Forest Service to cover the northern area. The construction of Halls Point in 1956 remedied the problem and the old Whetstone Lookout was burned in 1958.

name: Harl Butte Lookout
loc:
Wallowa-Whitman National Forest 
                    Wallowa County, Oregon
desc: The outrigger hip roof L-4 ground house without catwalk at Harl Butte was built in 1954, replacing another L-4 dating from 1934. The Wallowa-Whitman National Forest site overlooks the lower reaches of the Hells Canyon National Recreation Area and is in active service.

name: Harness Mountain Lookout
loc: Douglas County, Oregon
desc: Maintained and staffed by the Douglas Forest Protection Association Department of Forestry, Harness Mountain Lookout was first built in 1949 on a 40' tower and destroyed by the infamous Columbus Day storm in 1962. The following year the present 14' x 14' ODF flattop cab with catwalk on a 50' treated timber tower was constructed and continues in service.

name: Hat Point Lookout
loc:
Wallowa-Whitman National Forest 
                    Wallowa County, Oregon
desc: Hat Point Lookout on the Hells Canyon National Recreation Area (part of the Wallowa-Whitman National Forest) is a well known attraction and viewpoint. A 60' pole tower with 7'x7' cab was built in 1916. In 1948 it was replaced by this 82' treated timber tower with an L-6 7'x7' cab with catwalk. In the 1980s the tower was extensively restored with an observation deck added at the 60' level.

name: Henkle Butte Lookout
loc:
West Central Oregon 
                    Deschutes County, Oregon
desc: Located on a small hill north of Bend and surrounded by expensive homes, Henkle Butte Lookout may seem out of place, but is an active and effective fire detection point. Owned by the Oregon Dept. of Forestry, the first lookout was a ODF live in cab on a 40' tower. It was replaced with this 3 story ODF flattop cab in 1961.

name: Hershberger Lookout
loc:
Rogue River National Forest 
                    Douglas County, Oregon
desc: Hershberger Lookout is a cupola structure constructed in 1925. Also located on the Rogue River National Forest, it has not been actively staffed in recent years.

name: Hickman Butte Lookout
loc:
Mt. Hood National Forest 
                    Clackamas County, Oregon
desc: Located with the Bull Run Watershed of the Mt. Hood National Forest, few people have visited Hickman Lookout because access is only with an official escort. First established as a tent camp lookout in 1906, a 40' tower with 7' x 7' cab was built in 1933, with a ground quarters added later. In 1952 the current classic L-4 with catwalk on a 41' timber tower was constructed and remains in active service. It  is apparently the last L-4 lookout constructed in Oregon.

name: High Ridge Lookout
loc:
Umatilla National Forest 
                    Union County, Oregon
desc: One of the last sites developed on the Umatilla National Forest, High Ridge lookout was built in 1941 as an L-4 cab on a 24’ pole tower. In 1959 it was replaced with the present R-6 flattop cab with catwalk on a 67’ treated timber tower. Placed on standby status for awhile, it is now in active service.

name: Hogback Mountain Lookout
loc: Klamath County, Oregon
desc: Just to the east of Klamath Falls one can see Hogback Mountain Lookout. The first station was a 41’ tower built in 1941. Condemned in 1987, the Klamath Forest Protection Ass’n. and the Oregon Dept. of Forestry moved a 30’ steel tower with external stairway from Sycan Butte the following year and placed a new ODF low gable cab with catwalk on top. It is in active service.

name: Hoodoo Ridge Lookout
loc:
Umatilla National Forest 
                    Wallowa County, Oregon
desc: Hoodoo Ridge Lookout is a 100' steel Aermotor tower with 7'x7' cab built on the Umatilla National Forest around 1933. It is being evaluated for restoration as an historic site. This site was first used with a 65' tree crow's nest, which is still standing.

name: Horse Fly Mountain Lookout
loc:
Fremont National Forest 
                    Klamath County, Oregon
desc: Located on the Fremont National Forest on the east side of the Cascades in central Oregon, Horse Fly Mountain has two summits.  The original lookout was located on the southern point.  It was constructed of sawn timbers and boards. In 1934 the first tower on the northern point was constructed, an L-4 on a trestle type tower. In 1961 it was replaced with the current R-6 flattop cab with catwalk on a 41' treated timber tower. Placed on standby status in the 1970s, the lookout has been reactivated and staffed in recent years.

name: Huckleberry Mountain Lookout
loc:
Willamette National Forest 
                    Lane County, Oregon
desc: This L-4 ground house with catwalk was built in 1934 and is still in service. The original structure was restored by volunteers and the U.S. Forest Service in 1990 - 1991.

name: Illahee Rock Lookout
loc:
Umpqua National Forest 
                    Douglas County, Oregon
desc: Hikers to Oregon’s lllahee Rock Lookout in the Umpqua National Forest near Crater Lake National Park will also find an informal museum of lookout artifacts in the older cupola lookout (1922). The adjacent 20’ tower with 14’ x 14’ live-in cab and catwalk was constructed in 1955 and is still staffed each year. The cupola was shortened some years ago, but remains an example of the fast-disappearing D-6 structures.

name: Indian Ridge Lookout
loc:
Willamette National Forest 
                    Lane County, Oregon
desc: Located in the Willamette National Forest in Oregon’s central Cascade Mountains, Indian Ridge has been the site of a lookout since 1918. It is well known as the location of a classic 29’ “cathedral style” structure which remained in service until 1958 and regrettably was not maintained. No examples remain. The present 15’x 15’ R-6 flattop with catwalk on a 20’ wooden tower was built in 1957 and remained in service until 1973. It has been restored and is now available in the cabin rental system and is occasionally used for detection on an emergency basis. Scroll down to view photos of older cathedral-style structures.

name: Iron Mountain Lookout
loc:
Willamette National Forest 
                    Linn County, Oregon
desc:
Perched on a rock pinnacle above Highway 20 on the Willamette National Forest, Iron Mountain Lookout is a popular hiking and wildflower destination. A fire finder was placed on the site in 1929, followed by an L-4 ground house in 1933. The current R-6 flattop with catwalk was moved there in 1976.  This lookout was destroyed in 2007.
 

 
The lookout has been knocked down. Due to vandalism problems, they decided not to salvage the remaining items and to burn it in place.

name: Kelly Butte Lookout
loc: Douglas County, Oregon
desc: Kelly Butte Lookout in southwestern Oregon was built by the Weyerhaeuser Timber Company in 1950. The tall tower was constructed with 70' long logs with a L-4 cab with catwalk. In 2007 wood rot was discovered in one of the tower legs and the lookout was removed. There are no plans to reconstruct it.

name: King Mountain Lookout
loc:
Malheur National Forest 
                    Harney County, Oregon
desc: CL-100 model fire lookouts may not be pretty to look at, but they are very functional, surprisingly quiet in high winds, and low maintenance. That is why both the Park Service and BLM have adopted this Forest Service steel design with corrugated flat roof over the years. The lookout at King Mountain on the Malheur National Forest was built on the Ochocco National Forest in 1957 on a 10' steel tower. Previously the location had a D6 cupola built in the 1920s, followed by a cabin built in 1933. It will be listed on the National Lookout Register until it becomes 50 years old in 2007.

name: Lake of the Woods Lookout
loc:
Siskiyou National Forest 
                    Curry County, Oregon
desc: Three miles north of the Rogue River in the Siskiyou National Forest stands Lake of the Woods Lookout. First put into service in the 1920s as a tree crows nest until a L-4 cab was built in 1933. The present CL-160 metal flattop cab was first erected on Barkalow Mtn. in 1955 and moved to this site in 1974. Now atop an unusual steel I-beam 10’ tower, it is in the rental system.

name: Lava Butte Lookout
loc:
Deschutes National Forest 
                    Deschutes County, Oregon
desc: With this listing, Oregon becomes the first state to place 100 stations on the National Historic Lookout Register. The honor on Number 100 goes to Lava Butte Lookout on the Deschutes National Forest south of Bend, OR. One of the most visited lookouts in the U.S., the station is also a visitor center for the Lavalands National Monument. The current structure, the third on the site, was built in 1998 as a reproduction of a gable roof L-4 cab with catwalk. It replaced a unique slant window flattop cab with downstairs visitor center constructed in 1957. The original lookout was an L-4 groundhouse built in 1931.

name: Little Cowhorn Lookout
loc:
Willamette National Forest 
                    Lane County, Oregon
desc: Little Cowhorn Lookout on the Willamette National Forest was established in 1923 as a D6 cupola groundhouse. In 1960 it was replaced with a 14' x 14' R6 flattop on a short 4' wooden base. It remained in service only a few years before it was placed on standby status in 1967. Partially restored in the early 1990s, it is located on a popular trail near Eugene and is open for hiker use.

name: Little Grayback Mountain Lookout
loc:
Southwest Oregon 
                    Josephine County, Oregon
desc: The ODF flattop 14'x14' lookout on Little Grayback was moved to this site by the Oregon Dept. of Forestry from Waldo Hill in 1981. In active service, it is currently a study site for electronic fire detection systems.

name: Lookout Mountain Lookout
loc:
Umatilla National Forest 
                    Union County, Oregon
desc: This is the third Lookout Mountain Lookout to be listed on the NHLR, joining others in Idaho and Washington. Located on the Umatilla National Forest it first went into service in 1935 with a 60' wooden observation tower. The present L-4 with catwalk on an 87' timber tower was constructed in 1948. The cab was removed in 2004, restored on the site, and remounted by a crane.

name: Lookout Rock Lookout
loc:
Fremont National Forest 
                    Lake County, Oregon
desc: Aptly named (as it sits on top of a large rock), Lookout Rock Lookout was originally a crow's nest platform on the Fremont National Forest in the 1920s. It was replaced in 1932 with a 20' wooden tower with an L-4 cab. The present 14' x 14' R-6 flattop with catwalk on a 20' wood tower was constructed in 1962, but soon placed on standby status in 1968.

name: Morgan Butte Lookout
loc:
Fremont National Forest 
                    Lake County, Oregon
desc: Morgan Butte Lookout on the Fremont National Forest is relatively recent by western standards. The first structure on Morgan Butte was the Round Pass lookout house, which was moved by low-boy trailer in the spring of 1958. The current R-6 flattop groundhouse with catwalk was built in 1964. In 1985 it was rehabbed and a hip roof added.  The Round Pass site became an OMNI radar site and all duties were moved to Morgan Butte a short distance to the north.

name: Mount Pisgah Lookout
loc:
Ochoco National Forest 
                    Wheeler County, Oregon
desc: The 20’ wooden tower with a R-6 14’x14’ flattop live-in cab with catwalk was constructed in 1964. It is the fifth tower the Ochoco National Forest has built on this site. The first was a 10’ platform in 1919, followed in 1923 by a 35’ open platform tower with a ground cabin. In 1929 a cab was built on the platform. In 1933 a 20’ L-4 cab was constructed on a 20’ and served 31 years until the present lookout was built. It is in active service.

name: Mount Scott Lookout
loc:
Crater Lake National Park 
                    Klamath County, Oregon
desc: The other lookout in Crater Lake National Park, Mount Scott, can also claim a superlative: it is the highest-elevation lookout remaining in Oregon. The first structure on Mount Scott was constructed in 1924 and was a standard pre-cut wood cupola building. During the last 15 years of its existence, the building was so loose that plotting the location of a fire on a windy day was impossible. It was replaced in 1952 by the current two-story modified L-4 which has a unique fold-up catwalk. Reached by a scenic 2.5-mile trail, it is now maintained for emergency use.

name: Mount Stella Lookout
loc:
Rogue River National Forest 
                    Jackson County, Oregon
desc: Located to the west of Crater Lake National Park on the Rogue River National Forest, Mount Stella Lookout went into service as an L-4 on a 20’ pole tower in 1932. In 1947 it was replaced by a newer model L-4 on a 30’ treated timber tower. It has been on standby status since the mid 1980s.

name: Odell Butte Lookout
loc:
Deschutes National Forest 
                    Klamath County, Oregon
desc: Odell Butte was used as a patrol lookout as early as 1907. In 1915 it was established as an emergency lookout and used as such until the tower was constructed in the Fall of 1932.  A 12' x 12' frame cabin atop a log crib built in the 1920s. In 1932 it was replaced by a L-4 cab on a 20' tower. A R-6 live-in flattop cab with catwalk on a 30' treated wood tower was constructed in 1961 and continues in active service.

name: Olallie Mountain Lookout
loc:
Willamette National Forest 
                    Lane County, Oregon
desc:
Olallie Mountain Lookout leads off the second hundred listings in the NHLR. It is a very special place. Built in 1930 by the U.S. Forest Service, it is located at the head of French Pete Creek in the Willamette National Forest. The 14’ x 14’ L-4 ground house has not been staffed for many years. It is the site where the Oregon Lookout Association was founded in 1991. The group later became the largest state chapter of the Forest Fire Lookout Association. 
 The tower was in the process of being restored when it burned in 2019.

name: Onion Mountain Lookout
loc:
Siskiyou National Forest 
                    Josephine County, Oregon
desc: Developed about 1915 with a 20' platform tower, a D-6 cupola replaced it in 1924. An Aircraft Warning Service cabin was built in 1942. The present 10' treated timber L-4 tower, built in 1952, was staffed into the 1990s. It is available on the Recreation Rental program.

name: P-ranch Lookout
loc:
Malheur National Wildlife Refuge 
                    Harney County, Oregon
desc: Although closed to public access most of the year because of bird nesting habitat, P Ranch Lookout remains available for emergency use. The 72' Aermotor tower with 7' x 7' metal cab was constructed by the Civilian Conservation Corps in 1933.

name: Parker Mountain Lookout
loc: Klamath County, Oregon
desc: One of the newest fire lookouts in Oregon, Parker Mountain Lookout was built in 1997 replacing a historic 30’ tower constructed in 1934 and upgraded in 1958. The original lookout was a pole timber tower with an almost A-frame cab built by the CCC.  It had a very poor design. The second lookout was constructed on a steel tower with the standard ODF cab and was destroyed by vandals in 1996. This Oregon Dept. of Forestry station with 50’ steel tower with a 14’x14’ flattop cab and catwalk is still in active service.

name: Pearsoll Peak Lookout
loc:
Siskiyou National Forest 
                    Curry County, Oregon
desc: In 1954 the cupola style Pearsoll Peak lookout of the 1920s was replaced by the present L-4 style structure. In 1994 restoration efforts by Illinois Valley Ranger District and the Sand Mountain Society were completed.

name: Peavine Mountain Lookout
loc: Josephine County, Oregon
desc: The state lookout at Peavine Mountain in southern Oregon came to life as a rag camp in 1920, serving until an L-4 on a 40’ pole tower was constructed in 1933. In 1961 the present 14’x14’ flattop cab on a 41’ treated timber tower was built. This tower was condemned and burned to the ground on November 20, 2006.

name: Pechuck Mountain Lookout
loc:
Salem District 
                    Clackamas County, Oregon
desc: Pechuck Mountain, a former Oregon State Department of Forestry lookout located on Bureau of Land Management land near Molalla, has qualified as the second site to be registered. The structure is a cupola and is especially unique in that it was built of stone reminiscent of nearby Timberline Lodge on Mount Hood. Although not in use for many years, the building undoubtedly escaped razing because of the effort that would have been required to remove it. The building has been rerooted and restored by a group of volunteers led by Pete Bond, Trails Coordinator for the Oregon Department of State Parks in Salem.

name: Pelican Butte Lookout
loc:
Winema National Forest 
                    Klamath County, Oregon
desc:
Voted Oregon’s ugliest lookout by members of FFLA, Pelican Butte Lookout on the Winema National Forest nevertheless has a colorful history. 
 The first structure was an L-4 on a cable braced pole tower. In 1954 it was replaced by a classic new model L-4 on a treated timber tower, described in the book: “Walls of Glass.” Only 12 years later that was replaced by a R-6 live-in cab on a 20’ treated timber tower. 
 In 1986 a cable company requested use of the mountain top as a relay station, and proffered the present metal 10’x10’ cab on a 20’ metal tower as part of the bargain. Currently on standby status.

name: Pickett Butte Lookout
loc:
Umpqua National Forest 
                    Douglas County, Oregon
desc: Located in Southwest Oregon on the Umpqua National Forest, Pickett Butte Lookout is a classic 14' x 14' L-4 on a 41' timber tower. Carefully restored for the cabin rental program, it has remained in active service in the summer, while being available for rental in the non-fire season (the long wet winters). Because the fire finder and additional lookout paraphernalia remain present, renters are treated to a visit to an authentic historic site. Because it is in such demand as a rental, the district is also making it available during the summer during periods of low fire danger for fire lookout enthusiasts and others.

name: Pig Iron Lookout
loc:
Umpqua National Forest 
                    Douglas County, Oregon
desc:
Prefabricated by the Weyerhaeuser Sales Company in 1950, Pig Iron Lookout is probably one of a kind. No other examples of this kit have been identified. Similar to an L-4, the 10' x 10' cab has 3' x 3' solid pane windows and a catwalk atop a 10' wooden tower. This Umpqua National Forest lookout, located a half mile below the summit to get a better view, has been restored and it is used as an emergency detection site.
 

 
Former lookout Gary Wilson has contributed the following information:  "I manned this lookout in the summer of 1951. At that time I believe it was an L4 type cab. The usual paned windows were present and the shutter assembly opened up for shading. It was a brand new lookout which allowed me to do some painting and trimming of Douglas Fir trees felled to improve the view. In 2001 or so I visited the site and found the cab to look similar to the photo. There may have been a lookout structure at site before the current structure. A friend of mine served as a lookout the previous summer living in a tent near the site with an Osborne situated outside on a large log. He joked that he wore out his shoes on one side due to the steep slope he was working on. The current structure was built during this time and into the Fall of 1950."

name: Quail Prairie Lookout
loc:
Siskiyou National Forest 
                    Siskiyou County, Oregon
desc: While the giant Biscuit Fire burned for weeks in the summer of 2002, Quail Prairie Lookout saw it all. It is one of the most recent new lookout locations in southwestern Oregon on the Siskiyou National Forest. The R-6 flattop with live-in cab and catwalk is on a guyed 41' treated timber tower and is in active service.

name: Rajneesh Ranch Lookout
loc:
Big Creek Muddy Ranch 
                    Wasco County, Oregon
desc: Although one of the newest in Oregon, Rajneesh Lookout is by its own right historic. When the 64,229 acre Big Muddy Ranch was purchased in 1980 to become the cult city of Rajneeshpuram, life in the nearby ranching town of Antelope changed rapidly. Converts from all over the U.S. and distant lands of the world flocked to the emerging commune in remote Wasco County, many arriving from Portland on a newly certificated carrier, Air Rajneesh. In 1985 they built a unique two-story wooden ground house lookout with catwalk to watch for fires in the new community under construction. Then in the 1990s they left as quickly as they came. Much of the commune burned in subsequent wildfires and the lookout stands empty as a reminder of a tumultuous chapter of history that many Oregonians would just as soon forget.

name: Rancheria Rock Lookout
loc: Wheeler County, Oregon
desc: One of the most endangered sites in Oregon, Rancheria Rock Lookout is worth saving. The Oregon Department of Forestry model 14' x 14' cab was built in the 1950s, replacing an earlier structure dating from the 1930s. Located on BLM land, it is no longer in active service. There is interest in neighbors and the community in restoring it in association with a nearby state park. The Oregon Chapter of the FFLA is handling communications on the project.

name: Red Butte Lookout
loc:
Umpqua National Forest 
                    Douglas County, Oregon
desc: Red Butte Lookout on the west side of the Umpqua National Forest was the site of a L-4 cab on a 20' pole tower. It was replaced with the existing outrigger L-4 on a 41' treated timber tower in 1953. Used only in emergencies in recent years, the station is to be moved to Lookout Mountain in the future and possibly added to the cabin rental system.

name: Red Mountain Lookout
loc:
Umpqua National Forest 
                    Douglas County, Oregon
desc: The original lookout on Red Mountain was a tree tower built by the Umpqua National Forest in about 1920. It was replaced in 1928 with this D-6 12'x12' cupola cabin and staffed into the 1960s. Moved to the Tiller Ranger Station in 1985, it has been restored as an historic exhibit.

name: Riddle Mountain Lookout
loc:
East Central Oregon 
                    Harney County, Oregon
desc: This two-story concrete block and wooden frame live-in cab, built in 1964, is staffed during emergencies.

name: Ritter Butte Lookout
loc: Grant County, Oregon
desc: Located just off US 395 in Grant County, OR, Ritter Butte Lookout is also the station site of an engine on high fire days. The ODF 14’x14’ modified L-4 with a hip roof on a three story enclosed wooded tower with garage went into service in 1950.

name: Robinson Butte Lookout
loc:
Rogue River National Forest 
                    Jackson County, Oregon
desc: The first structure at Robinson Butte Lookout on the Rogue River National Forest was a rag camp in 1917. In 1933 a 20’ pole tower with L-4 cab was built, and replaced with the current 53’ timber tower with R-6 flat cab (from Blue Rock) in 1974.

name: Round Mountain Lookout
loc:
Deschutes National Forest 
                    Deschutes County, Oregon
desc: Round Mountain Lookout is a classic L-4 with upgraded catwalk on a low wood foundation atop a black lava knoll. Built in 1933, this Deschutes National Forest facility has been in service since then.

name: Round Top Lookout
loc: Jackson County, Oregon
desc: South of Grants Pass overlooking federal BLM land is Round Top Lookout. First put into service by the Oregon Dept. of Forestry in 1950 as an L-4 on a 20’ pole tower, it was replaced in 1973 with the current ODF flattop live-in cab with catwalk on a 20’ treated timber tower. It is in active service.

name: Rustler Peak Lookout
loc:
Rogue River National Forest 
                    Jackson County, Oregon
desc: Rustler Peak was a full fledged lookout in 1913 with William Parker as the first Lookout. In 1917 a pre-cut D-6 lookout house from the Mill-Made Construction Company of Portland was assembled in July. In the 1920s, a D-6 cupola on a 10’ tower was constructed. In 1940 the CCC expended $600 on lookout construction when the cupola was raised on a tower. The present L-4 14’x14’ cab with catwalk on a 31’6" laminated timber tower was built in 1948 and was the site of the first solar-powered radio system in a Forest Service lookout.

name: Saddleblanket Mountain Lookout
loc:
Willamette National Forest 
                    Lane County, Oregon
desc: In 1922 a crows nest was established in a 30-foot tall tree. The 70-foot tall Aermotor type LX-24 tower with a 7x7 cab was erected in 1927. This is the oldest lookout structure remaining on the National Forest and the only 6'x6' Aermotor constructed on the Forest. In 1939 the tower was modified by the installation of a stairway on the inside of the tower. Not many LX-24 Aermotors were built in Oregon. Another that comes to mind was at Slide Mountain in Lake County.

name: Sand Mountain Lookout
loc:
Willamette National Forest 
                    Linn County, Oregon
desc: Oregon Geographic Names says: Sand Mountain is a double summit about three miles south of the junction of US-20 and SH-22 west of Lost Lake. Each summit has a distinct crater and the whole is considered a textbook example of a cindercone occurring above a deep fissure. In the 1980s an effort was made to save the early USFS lookout. This culminated in the complete restoration of the building which now doubles as a lookout during high fire season and as an interpretive center for the regrowth of the area of the Big Lake Fire (Airstrip Burn) of 1967.

name: Scott Mountain Lookout
loc: Douglas County, Oregon
desc:
Scott Mountain located near Roseburg, Oregon has been used for fire detection continuously since 1912. The first lookout was a log cabin built in 1911. In 1933 it was replaced by a 100’ wooden tower which in turn was replaced in 1957 with the present 30’ ODF flatroof cab with catwalk. 
 The tower is maintained and staffed by the Douglas Forest Protective Association. 
  The lookout and related fire detection camera destroyed in the Archie Creek Fire in September 2020

name: Sexton Mountain Lookout
loc: Josephine County, Oregon
desc: There have been many Sexton Mountain Lookouts built by the Oregon Dept. of Forestry. The first was a tent in 1914, followed by a cupola cab ground house in 1921. In 1932 a small house with cupola was constructed and replaced with an ODF flat cab on a 30’ wooden tower in 1963. That lookout was burned by vandals in 2006 and replaced with this flat roof cab on 40’ steel tower in 2007.

name: Shitike Butte Lookout
loc:
Warm Springs Indian Reservation 
                    Jefferson County, Oregon
desc: The 90’Aermotor tower with 7’x7’ metal cab on Shitike Butte has watched over the pine forests of the Warm Springs Indian Reservation in central Oregon for 51 years and continues in active service.  Access is limited by regulations of the Warm Springs Tribe.

name: Sidwalter Mountain Lookout
loc:
Warm Springs Indian Reservation 
                    Wasco County, Oregon
desc: Located on the Warm Springs Indian Reservation, Sidwalter Mountain Lookout was constructed in 1967. It is a 107’ Aermotor tower with 7’x7’ metal cab on a section of the reservation closed to public access.

name: Signal Tree/kenyon Mountain Lookout
loc: Coos County, Oregon
desc: The first Kenyon (Signal Tree) Lookout was a cupola cabin built by the Coos Forest Protection Association in the 1920s. In 1935 a 100' timber tower with an L-6 cab replaced it. The present 53' treated wood tower with an Oregon Department of Forestry flatroof live-in cab was constructed in 1961 and is in active service.

name: Sisi Butte Lookout
loc:
Mt. Hood National Forest 
                    Clackamas County, Oregon
desc: SiSi Butte Lookout has long been an important detection point in the Oregon Cascades on the southern end of the Mt. Hood National Forest. In 1940 a L-4 with catwalk was built on a 41' timber tower. It was soon staffed year round as part of the Aircraft Warning Service in World War II. That structure was removed (with the historic parts salvaged) in 1977, replaced with a new generation fire tower. The octagonal cab with a catwalk/deck sits atop a 40' laminated wood tower. It is staffed each summer.

name: Snow Camp Lookout
loc:
Siskiyou National Forest 
                    Curry County, Oregon
desc: The first Lookout was constructed in 1917, and the present Lookout was constructed in 1958.

name: Snow Mountain Lookout
loc:
Malheur National Forest 
                    Grant County, Oregon
desc: Snow Mountain Lookout on the Ochocco National Forest in a 14’x14’ R-6 flattop live-in with catwalk on a 10’ treated timber tower. Staffed and in an area of high fire activity, it replaces a cupola lookout built in 1915 and an L-4 ground house constructed in 1930.

name: Sod House Lookout
loc:
Malheur National Wildlife Refuge 
                    Harney County, Oregon
desc: Located at the headquarters of the Malheur National Wildlife Refuge, Sod House Lookout was constructed by the Civilian Conservation Corps in 1933. The 80' Aermotor tower with 7' x 7' metal cab is still maintained for emergency use.

name: Soda Mountain Lookout
loc:
Cascade-Siskiyou National Monument 
                    Jackson County, Oregon
desc: Located on Bureau of Land Management (BLM) land on the eastern reach of the Siskiyou Range and four miles north of the California border, Soda Mountain Lookout was first a L-4 cab on 6' tower built in 1933. In 1962 the Oregon Dept. of Forestry replaced it with the present ODF 14' x 14' flat roof cab on a 10' tower. Still in active service, it is near the Pacific Crest Trail. Soda Mountain is included in the new Cascade-Siskiyou National Monument created by Presidential proclamation on June 1, 2000.

name: Spodue Mountain Lookout
loc:
Fremont National Forest 
                    Klamath County, Oregon
desc: The western-most lookout on the Fremont National Forest, Spodue Mountain Lookout (sometimes call Black Hills Lookout) first went into service in 1965 and remains active. It is a 15’x15’ R-6 flattop live-in cab with catwalk on a 41’ treated timber tower.

name: Spring Butte Lookout
loc:
Deschutes National Forest 
                    Klamath County, Oregon
desc: The new 41’ fire tower erected atop Spring Butte in the Deschutes National Forest in 1991 may be a prototype of things to come in the Pacific Northwest. The angled treated Douglas Fir pole tower is built to last. It is topped with a new 16’ x 16’ octagonal cab design with catwalk, and replaced an active L-4 pole tower dating from 1932.

name: Acorn Woman Peak Lookout
loc:
Rogue River National Forest 
                    Jackson County, Oregon
desc:
Used in early season before the snow recedes on nearby Dutchman Peak (US#19, OR#05) on the Rogue River National Forest, Squaw Peak Lookout is a classic new model L-4 groundhouse with catwalk. Build in 1943, it has been restored and is open to visitors. 
 9-22-26 The tower name has been updated from Squaw Peak Lookout to Acorn Woman Peak Lookout.  It was renamed approx 5 yrs ago.  The lookout is now available as a rental through  www.recreation.gov

name: Stephenson Mountain Lookout
loc: Jefferson County, Oregon
desc:
Stephenson Mountain Lookout, in Jefferson County, is also an ODF modified L-4 on an enclosed three story wooden tower and was built in 1963. The first lookout there was tree platform in 1931 which was replaced in 1934 with a 60’ wooden tower and ground house. 
 The tower was destroyed by the Box Springs Fire on July 20, 2026. 
  Update from the Brewer Fire Facebook page  
  At approximately 4:00 a.m. on July 20, 2026, intense fire activity on the Box Springs Fire reached Stephenson Lookout, resulting in the loss of the structure. This is a difficult moment for many across Central Oregon. Stephenson Lookout wasn’t just a tower on a ridge—it was a place rooted in community memory, wildfire history, and generations of fire detection that helped protect this landscape.    The first lookout was built on Stephenson decades ago, and from that vantage point, lookouts called in fires long before aircraft, satellites, or modern detection systems existed. The current tower—the fourth to stand on the site—was constructed in the 1960s. Although the site sits on Oregon Department of Forestry lands, it was transferred to the Ochoco National Forest in the late 1980s, where Forest Service personnel continued staffing and seasonal care.    In the days leading up to the fire’s arrival, crews completed mitigation work around the lookout and applied retardant, knowing the Box Springs Fire had the potential to push toward Stephenson Mountain. These actions were taken because of the lookout’s significance—both operationally and historically.    The site also included communication towers, which were impacted.     When the fire reached the site early on July 20, 2026, it did so with very high intensity. Extreme heat, heavy ember cast, and flame exposure overwhelmed the structure. Despite preparation efforts, conditions were simply too severe for the tower to withstand.    For many, Stephenson Lookout was more than a fire detection point. It was a place where lookouts learned their craft, where storms were tracked across the forest, and where countless fires were spotted early enough to help protect homes, rangelands, and timber. Its silhouette on Stephenson Mountain has been part of Central Oregon’s story for generations.    Losing a lookout means losing a piece of shared history. As suppression efforts continue on the Box Springs Fire, we honor the people—past and present—who dedicated their seasons to keeping watch from Stephenson and acknowledge the deep community ties to this landmark.    We will continue to share updates as they become available. Thank you for keeping firefighters and all those affected by the fires in Central Oregon in your thoughts.

name: Sugarloaf Mountain Lookout
loc:
Malheur National Forest 
                    Harney County, Oregon
desc: The first lookout on Sugarloaf Mountain was a 15' L-4 constructed in 1932. It was replaced in 1949 with the current L-4 with catwalk on a 32' wooden tower. The Malheur National Forest site is in active service.

name: Table Rock Lookout
loc:
Wallowa-Whitman National Forest 
                    Baker County, Oregon
desc: A classic early lookout site in eastern Oregon, Table Rock’s first structure, Table Rock Lookout began as a cupola built in the early 1920s. It was replaced with a 14’ x 14’ L-4 cab with catwalk in 1937, and again with a new L-4 in 1949. Still in active service it is located in the southern tip of the Wallowa-Whitman National Forest in the Monument Rock Wilderness.

name: Tallowbox Lookout
loc: Jackson County, Oregon
desc: Standing on a high promontory with a long ranging view south of Medford is Tallowbox Lookout. The Oregon Dept. of Forestry lookout was a tent camp in 1918. The first permanent building was a cupola lookout in 1923. During World War II the garage was converted into an Aircraft Warning Service winter residence and the site staffed year around. The current 14’x14’ ODF flattop with catwalk on a 10’ treated timber tower was constructed in 1963 and remains in active service.

name: Tiptop Mountain Lookout
loc:
Northeast Oregon 
                    Umatilla County, Oregon
desc: Tiptop Mountain Lookout near the old Oregon Trail in the Blue Mountains was an L4 cab on a 15' pole tower built by the state in the 1930s. In 1961 this 14'x14' ODF flattop cab was erected on a 40' steel tower. Now surplus, it is slated for removal if not adopted by a partner organization soon.

name: Tope Creek Lookout
loc: Wallowa County, Oregon
desc: The fourth privately-owned tower to be listed, Tope Creek Lookout, was constructed by the U.S. Forest Service in 1936 and later transferred to the Oregon Department of Forestry. It was staffed until the early 1970s, when it was declared surplus. The 103’ timber tower with 8’x 8’ L-6 cab with catwalk has been restored by Brian Wizard, the current owner.

name: Tower Mountain Lookout
loc:
Umatilla National Forest 
                    Umatilla County, Oregon
desc: One of the few 7’x7’ steel towers ever erected in the Umatilla National Forest in northeastern Oregon, Tower Mountain Lookout, remains in service today. The 92’ tower was constructed by the U.S. Forest Service in 1929, and the attractive CCC cabin living quarters was moved to the site from the old Lucky Strike Lookout in the late 1940s.

name: Trout Creek Butte Lookout
loc:
Deschutes National Forest 
                    Deschutes County, Oregon
desc: One of a handful of 7’x7’ Aermotor towers remaining in the central Cascades, the 86’ Trout Creek Butte Lookout has stood on the Deschutes National Forest since 1933. It has been on standby status since 1972.

name: Wagontire Mountain Lookout
loc:
East Central Oregon 
                    Harney County, Oregon
desc: This two-story BLM concrete block and wooden frame live-in cab, built in 1967 as the first and only lookout structure on the summit, is staffed every summer.

name: Waldo Mountain Lookout
loc:
Willamette National Forest 
                    Lane County, Oregon
desc: Located within the Waldo Lake Wilderness -- Willamette National Forest -- on the crest of the Cascade Mountains, Waldo Mountain Lookout is a 15’x15’ R-6 flattop ground house constructed in 1957. It replaced a D-6 cupola lookout built in 1929 which itself was a replacement for a pole and shake structure erected three years earlier. The station is still staffed on an emergency basis during lightning storms.

name: Walker Mountain Lookout
loc:
Deschutes National Forest 
                    Klamath County, Oregon
desc: Walker Mountain was used as a patrol lookout as early as 1907, by 1913 a crows nest was established in a tree. In 1915 the stone cabin, used for living quarters, was begun and by the end of the season was fully enclosed. In 1919 a pole tower approximately 25 feet tall with a small 6x6 windowless cab was erected. In 1932 a road was constructed to the summit and the new steel tower construction was begun in the Fall and not completed until the next year (1933). Both are intact and maintained. The 35 steel tower with hip-roof L-4 14’x14 cab with catwalk was constructed in 1932. The stone cabin was restored in 2005.

name: Wanoga Butte Lookout
loc:
High Desert Museum 
                    Deschutes County, Oregon
desc: Built in 1932, Wanoga Butte Lookout is another vintage L-4 hip-roof cab with catwalk atop a 30’ pole tower located on the Deschutes National Forest in central Oregon. The garage was built in 1933. The original ponderosa pine tower legs were replaced with tamarack poles in 1953. During a period of time from July 10 and July 15, 2006, a crew of volunteers dismantled the tower. The cabin was bundled and stored at the High Desert Museum for later reconstruction. The tower was cut up and all hardware salvaged for future restorations and was moved to the High Desert Museum in 2006.

name: Warner Mountain Lookout
loc:
Willamette National Forest 
                    Lane County, Oregon
desc: Every now and then a classic lookout structure appears in the nominations for listing in the National Historic Lookout Register, and Warner Mountain Lookout on the Willamette National Forest is one of them. Although of recent construction (1987), the 41' tower is historically unique in the U.S. The 14'x14' live-in cab is a replica of the cupola design of the 1920s. Most of the cupola buildings were on the ground and a few were on short crib structures. This is the only one know to have been placed on top of a 41' tower.

name: Watchman Lookout
loc:
Crater Lake National Park 
                    Klamath County, Oregon
desc: One of the grandest lookouts in Oregon, if not the U.S., The Watchman is located at the edge of the Crater Lake caldera overlooking the lake itself. The imposing two-story stone structure was built by crews under the supervision of the U.S. National Park Service in 1931 and was completed in the early part of the fire season in 1932. Reached by a short hike from the west rim overlook, it is possibly the most visited lookout in Oregon (Lava Butte may claim that title). Carefully restored in 1999, the lookout is in service.

name: West Myrtle Butte Lookout
loc:
Malheur National Forest 
                    Grant County, Oregon
desc: When West Myrtle Butte Lookout was downgraded to emergency use status, the Malheur National Forest placed the ground living quarters on the cabin rental system to provide income for upkeep of the tower. The 67' steel structure with 7' x 7' metal cab dates back to 1928.

name: White Point Lookout
loc: Jackson County, Oregon
desc: Unusual in that it is only two miles south of Halls Point Lookout (US#491, OR#94) and both are in active service, White Point Lookout sees a wide area to the south. In 1951 it was an L-4 on a 40’ tower. In 1974, the Oregon Dept. of Forestry built the current 14’x14’ ODF flattop live-in cab with caltwalk on a 30’ treated timber tower.

name: Wildhorse Mountain Lookout
loc:
Siskiyou National Forest 
                    Curry County, Oregon
desc: Wildhorse Lookout on the Siskiyou National Forest is occasionally staffed by either the USFS or the Coos Forest Protective Ass’n. Built in 1947, it is a new model L-4 with catwalk on a 40’ treated timber tower. Earlier structures on the site were an L-4 on a 40’ pole in 1935 and an Aircraft Warning Service house during World War II.

name: Wolf Mountain Lookout
loc:
Ochoco National Forest 
                    Wheeler County, Oregon
desc:
The first lookout on this site was a 50' wooden L-6 tower and cabin one mile west of the present tower. In 1932 a crow's nest was erected one mile east, which is still standing. 
 The present 107' treated timber L-4 tower, built in 1947, is staffed every summer and still uses the old phone system with radio backup. The lookout oversees the Black Canyon Wilderness and the east end of the Ochoco National Forest.

name: Yellow Butte Lookout
loc: Douglas County, Oregon
desc: This lookout was removed about 2016.

name: Tamarack Mountain Lookout
loc:
Umatilla National Forest 
                    Grant County, Oregon
admin: US Forest Service - Umatilla National Forest
desc:
The original Tamarack Lookout for forest fire detection on this site was a platform built in a tree back in 1925. The current 96' steel Aermotor tower replaced the glorified tree fort in 1933.   
  Tamarack Lookout Cabin, the housing for Forest Service personnel using the lookout for fire detection, was built in 1934. An accidental fire destroyed the cabin in 1966, and a garage/utility shed was then converted into the existing cabin. The cabin is now available for rental.   
  The Friends of Blue Mountain Lookouts completed a stair replacement project in September 2021.  
  Tamarack Lookout is staffed irregularly.

name: Bald Knob Lookout
loc:
Siskiyou National Forest 
                    Coos County, Oregon
admin: US Forest Service - Siskiyou National Forest
desc:
The original structure at Bald Knob was built in 1914. 
 Bald Knob served as an Aircraft Warning Service site in 1942-43 
 The current structure is an R-6 Flattop cabin on a 20 foot wood tower was constructed in 1963 and is available for nightly rental.

name: Bone Point Lookout
loc:
Umatilla National Forest 
                    Grant County, Oregon
desc:
The current 30-feet steel live-in tower at Bone Point is the fourth tower at this location. It remains for emergency use and was last staffed in 2003 for a brief period of lightning storms. 
 Prior towers at this site include a cupola cabin used in the 1920s, a 40-foot wood live-in tower in the 1930s, and a 30-foot steel live-in tower built in 1947.

name: Bear Butte Lookout
loc: Klamath County, Oregon
desc:
Bear Butte, also known as Baldy or Bear Flat was constructed for the Klamath Forest Protective Association in 1949 replacing an earlier structure dating to at least 1930. The structure is located on Weyerhaeuser Company land. 
 The lookout was last staffed in 1966.

name: Big Lookout Mountain
loc:
Vale District - Bureau of Land Management 
                    Baker County, Oregon
desc:
A BLM design cabin similar to the USFS R6 Flat Top on a 10 foot block, enclosed tower. The structure was built in 1963. 
 Temporary lookouts were placed on the mountain in 1957 until the permanent structure was built.

name: Big Rock Lookout
loc:
Private Land 
                    Linn County, Oregon
desc:
Big Rock was built in 1950, a standard USFS BC-301 design cabin on a 9 foot enclosed tower. 
 The lookout was built by the Santiam Lumber Company and staffed by the Linn County Fire Patrol. One of several lookouts with this arrangement.

name: Bryant Mountain Lookout
loc:
Private Land 
                    Klamath County, Oregon
desc:
Bryant Mountain was constructed in 1981 replacing an earlier structure destroyed by wildfire in 1979. 
 The cabin is a BLM flat top design on a 30 foot open timber tower. 
 The lookout structure was transferred to the land owner in 2007.

name: Buckhorn Mountain Lookout
loc:
Wallowa-Whitman National Forest 
                    Wallowa County, Oregon
admin: US Forest Service - Wallowa-Whitman National Forest
desc:
Buckhorn Mountain is a standard US Forest Service L-4 ground cabin and catwalk on short stone aggregate piers. 
  The lookout cab from the Fairchild tower was lowered and moved to the Buckhorn Mountain site in 1952. Original date of construction is unknown.

name: Desolation Butte Lookout
loc:
Umatilla National Forest 
                    Grant County, Oregon
admin: US Forest Service - Umatilla National Forest
desc:
Desolation Butte was constructed in 1961 replacing an earlier 1923 built 7x7 cabin on a 50 foot open steel tower. 
 The lookout is an USFS R6 Flat Top cabin design on a 67 foot open timber tower.

name: Elk Mountain Lookout
loc:
Wallowa-Whitman National Forest 
                    Union County, Oregon
admin: US Forest Service - Wallowa-Whitman National Forest
desc:
Elk Mountain was built in 1933, an L-4 cabin on a tower reported variably at 10 to 40 feet. 
 The cabin was removed from the tower sometime in the 1960's and continued to be staffed until 1972. 
 The lookout is located on private land and not accessible to the public.

name: Garwood Butte Lookout
loc:
Umpqua National Forest 
                    Douglas County, Oregon
admin: US Forest Service - Umpqua National Forest
desc:
Garwood Butte was constructed in 1942, an updated BC-301 version of the classic L-4 cabin. 
 The lookout was no longer staffed after 1973.

name: Gerow Butte Lookout
loc:
Private Land 
                    Crook County, Oregon
desc:
The current tower and cabin were built in 1968 replacing the 1934 built structures. 
 Gerow Butte is an R6 Flat Top cabin atop a 60 foot open timber tower. 
 The lookout is located on private land not accessible to the public.

name: Green Mountain Lookout
loc:
Lakeview District - Bureau of Land Management 
                    Lake County, Oregon
desc:
Green Mountain is a unique BLM design, a 50-foot block tower and cabin constructed in 2011 using funds from the American Recovery and Reinvestment Act of 2009. 
 This block tower replaced an earlier 1963 tower with a 10-foot two-story concrete base topped by a wood live-in cab.

name: Grizzly Mountain Lookout
loc: Curry County, Oregon
desc:
A 14 x 14 Amort style lookout house was constructed in 1952, replacing a 1942 structure.   
  The original 1937 lookout was destroyed in a 1942 storm.  
  The site served as an Aircraft Warning Service site during World War 2.

name: Hager Mountain Lookout
loc:
Fremont National Forest 
                    Lake County, Oregon
admin: US Forest Service - Fremont National Forest
desc:
Hager Mountain has been a fire detection site since 1915. 
 The current structure was constructed in 1967, an R6 Flat Top ground cabin. The roof was modified with a slight hip roof in 1992.

name: Halfway Lookout
loc:
Wallowa-Whitman National Forest 
                    Baker County, Oregon
admin: US Forest Service - Wallowa-Whitman National Forest
desc:
Halfway Lookout is a 7x7 observation only cab and catwalk on a 52 foot open timber tower. 
 The tower was constructed in 1938 at the  Wallowa-Whitman National Forest Pine Field Office.  
  It can be used in case of emergencies.

name: Howard Butte Lookout
loc:
Northeast Oregon District - Oregon Department of Forestry 
                    Wallowa County, Oregon
desc:
Howard Butte was constructed in 1941 by the Civilian Conservation Corps. 
 The structure is a 7x7 observation only cab and catwalk on a 100 foot open timber tower. A small residence cabin was built as well.

name: Indian Rock Lookout
loc:
Malheur National Forest 
                    Grant County, Oregon
admin: US Forest Service - Malheur National Forest
desc:
Indian Rock was constructed in 1957 replacing an earlier structure built in 1929. 
 The structure is a USFS R6 Flat Top ground cabin.

name: Johnson Rock Lookout
loc:
Wallowa-Whitman National Forest 
                    Union County, Oregon
admin: US Forest Service - Wallowa-Whitman National Forest
desc:
Johnson Rock was constructed in 1952. The structure is an 82 foot open timber tower topped by a 14x14 L-4 cab. 
 The current replaces an earlier L-4 built in 1938.

name: Long Ridge Lookout
loc:
Private Land 
                    Wallowa County, Oregon
desc:
Long Ridge Lookout was constructed in 1959 & 60 on Tiptop Mountain.  
 The structure was acquired and moved to private land in 2016.

name: Mackay Butte Lookout
loc:
Private Land 
                    Crook County, Oregon
desc:
The lookout is generally referred to as 'Mackey Butte Lookout' in contemporary media reports. Period photos show signage stating 'Norcross Forest Guard Station'. 
 A camp was established in 1925. A residence cabin and garage were built along with an exposed fire-finder stand were completed in 1935. The fire-finder was enclosed in 6x6 ground lookout house in 1940. 
 The station was abandoned in the 1950's and as of 2019, is still a standing ruin.

name: Madison Butte Lookout
loc:
Umatilla National Forest 
                    Morrow County, Oregon
admin: US Forest Service - Umatilla National Forest
desc:
Madison Butte was built in 1957 replacing a 1923 D-6 Cupola ground cab.  
 The 13x13 Plan CL-100 cab stands on a 37 foot K-Brace steel tower.

name: McGraw Mountain Lookout
loc:
Wallowa-Whitman National Forest 
                    Wallowa County, Oregon
admin: US Forest Service - Wallowa-Whitman National Forest
desc:
McGraw Mountain Lookout is a 14x14 Region 6 Flat Top cab on a 82 foot open timber tower. The structure was built in 1965. 
 The site has been used for fire detection since at least 1930. An L-4 cab on a 10 foot pole tower was built in 1934.

name: Mount Harris Lookout
loc: Union County, Oregon
desc:
Mount Harris first hosted a lookout in 1930. The original tower was replaced sometime later in the 30's. 
 The current structure was built at a slightly different location in 1957, a live in cab on a 40 foot open timber tower.

name: Mount Ireland Lookout
loc:
Wallowa-Whitman National Forest 
                    Grant County, Oregon
admin: US Forest Service - Wallowa-Whitman National Forest
desc:
A cabin with an open roof for a fire-finder was built on Mount Ireland in 1916. The fire-finder was later enclosed. 
 The new CL-100 13x13 ground cab was constructed in 1957 after blasting the old structure off the mountain. 
 The lookout is regularly staffed.

name: Mule Peak Lookout
loc:
Wallowa-Whitman National Forest 
                    Union County, Oregon
admin: US Forest Service - Wallowa-Whitman National Forest
desc:
Mule Peak was selected as a fire detection site in 1916. The site was staffed and communication was by heliograph. 
 The current D-5 cab may have been constructed as early as 1924.  
 The lookout received a new cedar shake roof and paint in 2021.

name: Prairie City Lookout
loc:
Prairie City, Oregon 
                    Grant County, Oregon
admin: US Forest Service - Malheur National Forest
desc:
An Osborne fire-finder is located in an enclosure just south of Prairie City, Oregon. The fire-finder has been in use their since some time in the 1930's. 
 The valley area is surrounded by mountain ranges on three sides and is used as needed. 
 A new lockbox was installed some time between 2016 and 2018.

name: Point Prominence Lookout
loc:
Wallowa-Whitman National Forest 
                    Union County, Oregon
admin: US Forest Service - Wallowa-Whitman National Forest
desc:
The current 82 foot open timber tower and live in cab were completed in 1954 a short distance from the previous tower location. 
 A lookout was first completed in 1916 on a 50 foot tower with fire-finder. It was replaced in 1931 by an L-4 cab on a 30 foot pole tower.

name: Russel Mountain Lookout
loc:
Wallowa-Whitman National Forest 
                    Baker County, Oregon
admin: US Forest Service - Wallowa-Whitman National Forest
desc:
Russel Mountain has been a fire detection site since 1921 with an open platform on a 50 foot tower. A small observation only cab was added later. 
 The current 82 foot open timber tower was constructed in 1949. The L-4 cab was added in 1950.

name: South Baldy Lookout
loc: Wheeler County, Oregon
desc:
The current South Baldy Lookout was constructed in 1958-59, a 14x14 L-4 cab atop a 40 foot open timber tower. 
 The site as served fire detection since at least 1936. 
 South Baldy was staffed to at least 1964.

name: Sugarpine Mountain Lookout
loc:
Winema National Forest 
                    Klamath County, Oregon
admin: US Forest Service - Winema National Forest
desc:
The Sugarpine Lookout structure was relocated from Fort Klamath in 1970. The structure was originally built in 1958. 
 The lookout is a 20 foot X-Brace, open steel tower with a 13x13 Plan CL-100 cab atop.

name: Summit Point Lookout
loc:
Wallowa-Whitman National Forest 
                    Baker County, Oregon
admin: US Forest Service - Wallowa-Whitman National Forest
desc:
Summit Point was constructed in 1949, replacing an earlier open platform tower. 
 The structure is a 20 foot open timber tower with a 14x14 L-4 cab atop.

name: Table Mountain Lookout
loc:
Southwest Oregon District, Oregon Department of Forestry 
                    Jackson County, Oregon
desc:
The first lookout was placed at Table Mountain in 1930 by the Klamath National Forest. 
 The current structure was constructed in 1958, a 30 foot open timber tower with an R-6 Flat Top cab. 
 The lookout was staffed until at least 1975. The structure is on private property with no public access.

name: Tower Point Lookout
loc:
Ochoco National Forest 
                    Crook County,, Oregon
admin: US Forest Service - Ochoco National Forest
desc:
Tower Point was constructed in 1955, an L-4 cab on a 20 foot open timber tower. 
 The site began use for fire detection in 1919. A timber tower was erected in 1940.

name: Unity Lookout
loc:
Wallowa-Whitman National Forest 
                    Baker County, Oregon
admin: US Forest Service - Wallowa-Whitman National Forest
desc:
The lookout is located on the Unity Ranger Station in the community of Unity, Oregon. 
 The 60 foot open timber tower with a 6x6 observation cab was built in 1938.

name: Yainax Butte Lookout
loc:
Klamath Agency 
                    Klamath County, Oregon
desc:
A 21-foot steel Aermotor model LS-40 Aermotor tower with a 7 x 7 steel cab was constructed in 1930 by the Klamath Forest Protective Association.  
  A residence cabin was added in 1936, The lookout was staffed into the 1970's.

name: Sycan Marsh Lookout
loc:
Private Land 
                    Lake County, Oregon
admin: US Forest Service - Fremont National Forest
desc:
The lookout was constructed in 1933. The structure is a 6x6 cab on open pole tower. 
 The site is on private land and not accessible to the public.

name: Red Hill Lookout
loc:
Wallowa-Whitman National Forest 
                    Wallowa County, Oregon
admin: US Forest Service - Wallowa-Whitman National Forest
desc:
The current Red Hill Lookout was completed in 1949, a 40 foot open timber tower with an L-4 cab on top. 
 Red Hill has been a fire detection site since 1917, first with a pole platform then a 10x10 cab on an open timber tower.

name: Craft Point Lookout
loc:
Malheur National Forest 
                    Harney County, Oregon
desc: This lookout was built in 1930 as a 15-foot platform observation tower. It was abandoned in the 1940s. The platform was still standing as of May 30, 2021.

name: Apgar Lookout
loc:
Glacier National Park 
                    Flathead County, Montana
desc: Apgar Lookout overlooks the Lake McDonald region.  It is a two-story wooden structure with an enclosed 10-ft tower and 14- by 14-ft cab.  This is one of two basic designs found in the Park.  The first lookout was constructed on the site in 1929 and was destroyed by fire two weeks after completion.  This identical structure was built in 1930.  Located a mile high, it is the lowest elevation lookout in the Park.

name: Baptiste Lookout
loc: Flathead County, Montana
desc:
The current Baptiste Lookout was built in 1964 on a ridge west of Mt. Baptiste as a replacement for a 1928 30' tower. It was staffed annually until 1971 with minimal maintenance thereafter. In 2005 due to vandalism and liability concerns, the lower stairs were removed.
 
 
 
In 2010 the USFS conducted a site assessment with rehabilitation work starting in 2011; expected to be complete in the fall of 2013.  Annual volunteer staffing started in 2012.

name: Bare Cone Lookout
loc:
Bitterroot National Forest 
                    Ravalli County, Montana
desc: Still in active service on the Bitterroot National Forest, Bare Cone Lookout was first a two story log cabin in 1922. In the 1930s an L-4 was built on a 10’ tower which served until the present R-6 cab with catwalk on a 10’ concrete block base was built in 1962.

name: Barren Peak Lookout
loc:
Kootenai National Forest 
                    Lincoln County, Montana
desc: Built in 1940, this 10' wooden tower with L-4 cab replaced an earlier camp. John M. Richards manned this lookout in the summers of 1944-45, during World War II. The lookout has been abandoned since the 1970s.

name: Berray Mountain Lookout
loc:
Kootenai National Forest 
                    Sanders County, Montana
desc: Berray Mountain Lookout was a rough-hewn crow’s nest tower with an attractive log cabin and porch for living quarters built in 1931. lt was replaced in 1940 with an L-4 lookout on a 50’ pole tower. The present R-6 Flattop with catwalk on a 30’ timber tower was constructed in 1965, but has seen little use since the 1970s.

name: Big Creek Baldy Lookout
loc:
Kootenai National Forest 
                    Lincoln County, Montana
desc: As the U.S. Forest Service was developing a fire detection system on the Kootenai National Forest in the northwestern corner of Montana, Big Creek Baldy was an obvious location. The first structure was a log cabin built in 1929 which is still there (in need of repair). It was supplemented with a 30' wood tower with small 7' x 7' cab in 1934 to get a better view, and in 1966 a higher 41' timber live-in tower with 15' x 15' flattop cab was built. The lookout is available in the rental program.

name: Big Hole Lookout
loc:
Lolo National Forest 
                    Sanders County, Montana
desc: Big Hole Lookout on the Lolo National Forest is only one of a few log/frame lookouts remaining. In need of restoration, it was built in 1930 and staffed until 1972. Access is still only by trail.

name: Blue Mountain Lookout
loc:
Kootenai National Forest 
                    Lincoln County, Montana
desc: Located in the Purcell Mountains on the Kootenai National Forest, Blue Mountain Lookout was used as a lookout point in the early 1920s. In 1928 a one-room residence ground house was built, followed in 1935 with a 80' steel tower with 7' x 7' metal cab erected by the CCC. In 1940 a new ground house was constructed. The tower and ground living quarters remain in active service.

name: Blue Mountain Lookout
loc:
Lolo National Forest 
                    Missoula County, Montana
desc: Blue Mountain is the last remaining active lookout on the Missoula Ranger District of the Lob National Forest. The 41’ wooden tower with 15’ x 15’ flattop cab was originally constructed on Davis Point, where it was used in filming “Red Skies of Montana.” At that time the movie company paid for the modified slanted glass windows to reduce glare. In 1966 it was moved to its present location.

name: Boulder Point Lookout
loc:
Bitterroot National Forest 
                    Ravalli County, Montana
desc: Restoration activities were completed on Boulder Point lookout in July, 2003 by the West Fork Ski Club along with both active and retired Forest Service personnel from the Bitterroot National Forest. The historic L-4 cab with catwalk on an 10’ pole tower was built in 1937 and in service until the 1980s. The historic site is popular with locals as both a summer hike and winter ski-in destination.

name: Cinnamon Mountain Lookout
loc:
Gallatin National Forest 
                    Gallatin County, Montana
desc: Cinnamon Mountain Lookout on the Gallatin National Forest was constructed by the U.S. Forest Service in 1958. Since it is not quite 50 years old, it will be listed on the National Lookout Register until 2008, when it will be transferred to the National Historic Lookout Register. It was the site of a "rag camp" (tent) lookout in the 1930s until the R-6 flattop cab with catwalk on a 10' wood tower went into service. It was rehabilitated in 1999.

name: Cougar Peak Lookout
loc:
Lolo National Forest 
                    Sanders County, Montana
desc: The current Cougar Peak lookout, built in 1952, is the only standard 1936-model hip-roof L-4 ground house with catwalk on the Lolo National Forest. This structure replaced an L-4 cab with gable roof built in 1930. Cougar overlooks the Clark Fork River Valley and has a spectacular view of the Cabinet Mountains Wilderness. Cougar was last regularly staffed in the mid-1980's, and is currently on the cabin rental program. An interesting aspect of Cougar Peak is the unique rock art created by former lookouts. The earliest rock inscription is dated 1921, surrounded by numerous other rock carvings of names, dates, and artwork by lookouts of the past. A 1995 Passport in Time project saw the reroofing of the lookout, and the replacing and repairing of windows and the door, as well as other repairs.

name: Deer Mountain Lookout
loc:
Bitterroot National Forest 
                    Ravalli County, Montana
desc: A log cupola cabin built in 1926 was the first Deer Mountain Lookout on the Bitterroot National Forest. This 15'x15' R-6 cab with catwalk on a 10' concrete base replaced it in 1960.

name: Double Arrow Lookout
loc:
Lolo National Forest 
                    Missoula County, Montana
desc: Located on a low hill near Seeley Lake, Montana, Double Arrow lookout was built in 1932 before a road led to the site. It is an L-4 cab with catwalk atop a 20’ slanting pole tower. Used only on an emergency basis since 1989, it is popular with valley residents as a viewpoint.

name: Eddy Mountain Lookout
loc:
Lolo National Forest 
                    Sanders County, Montana
desc: The first station at Eddy Mountain Lookout on the Lolo National Forest was a standard gable-roof L-4 ground house built in 1931. The present R-6 flattop, 15’x15’ with catwalk on a 10’ concrete base was constructed in 1982 and is one of the newest lookout structures in the region. Eddy Peak (and the town of Eddy, Montana) was named after Richard Eddy, one of the owners of the Eddy-Hammond Company, later known as the Missoula Mercantile Company, in 1885. Eddy Peak has been a primary lookout for the district since the 1930's and is still staffed every season.

name: Firefighter Lookout
loc:
Flathead National Forest 
                    Flathead County, Montana
desc: Firefighter Lookout is an L-4 cab on a 41' timber tower built in 1953 on the Flathead National Forest. Later its hip roof was replaced with a flat roof with 3' overhang. It replaced a log cabin cupola lookout.

name: Garver Mountain Lookout
loc:
Kootenai National Forest 
                    Lincoln County, Montana
desc: An impressive feature of Garver Mountain Lookout is the 1929 log ground house which is still in relatively good condition. It was supplemented three years later with a 48' pole tower with 6' x 6' wood cab and catwalk. In 1964 a helispot and the present 30' timber tower with 14' x 14' flattop cab and catwalk were constructed. Used for detection until 1979, the cabin and lookout are being restored and will be placed in the Kootenai National Forest rental system in 2002.

name: Gem Peak Lookout
loc:
Kootenai National Forest 
                    Sanders County, Montana
desc: Gem Peak Lookout was activated in 1921 as a U.S. Forest Service “rag outfit” -- a pole platform tent near an open platform tower and remained that way nearly two decades until an L-4 on a 20 pole tower was built in 1939. In 1964 the present R-6 Flattop cab with catwalk on 30 timber tower was constructed and staffed through the 1970s. It is now one of three rental lookouts on the Cabinet Ranger District.

name: Gird Point Lookout
loc:
Bitterroot National Forest 
                    Ravalli County, Montana
desc: In 1984 Gird Point and seven other inactive lookouts on the Bitterroot and Lolo National Forests were slated for removal. Happily three were saved from destruction and restored. Built in 1939, this L-4 live-in cab on an 8' timber tower was rehabilitated in 2002. It is now in the cabin rental system.

name: Granite Butte Lookout
loc:
Helena National Forest 
                    Lewis and Clark County, Montana
desc: Granite Butte Lookout is one of only four remaining on the Helena National Forest. The first lookout on this site was an L-4 cab on a 20’ tower built in 1932. This 15’x15’ R-6 flat cab on a treated wood tower was constructed in 1962.

name: Heavens Peak Lookout
loc:
Glacier National Park 
                    Flathead County, Montana
desc: Heaven's Peak Lookout is a unique stone and wood structure designed for the rocky, windswept site. Built in 1945 by concientious objecters during World War II, it is the newest in the Park. With a stone foundation and stone wall catwalk, the 12'x12' cab has a flat roof.

name: Highland Lookout
loc:
Beaverhead-Deerlodge National Forest 
                    Silver Bow County, Montana
desc: Built in 1954 on the Beaverhead-Deerlodge National Forest, Highland Lookout is a L-4 cab with catwalk on a one story concrete base. It replaced an L-4 groundhouse built in 1933.

name: Hornet Peak Lookout
loc:
Flathead National Forest 
                    Flathead County, Montana
desc: Hornet Peak Lookout was built in 1922. It has a D-1 log cupola cabin. While it was abandoned for a number of years, it has now been restored and available for rental.

name: Horse Butte Lookout
loc:
Gallatin National Forest 
                    Gallatin County, Montana
desc: The first improvement at Horse Mountain Lookout on the Gallatin National Forest was a crow’s nest platform put up in the 1920s which is still there. The current 14’x14’ L-4 live-in cab on a 41’ timber tower was constructed in 1953.

name: Huckleberry Lookout
loc:
Glacier National Park 
                    Flathead County, Montana
desc: Huckleberry Lookout is a 14'x14' wooden structure similar to Apgar, but of a second design with the hip roof extended to cover the catwalk. The basic design differs from Forest Service L-4s in that the shutters are removable and do not fold up for shading. An original cupola lookout on the site was replaced by this structure in 1933.

name: Keeler Mountain Lookout
loc:
Kootenai National Forest 
                    Lincoln County, Montana
desc: The current Keeler Mountain Lookout is a 53-foot treated lumber R-6 tower. It is the third lookout at the site. The original 1924 lookout was a 50-foot platform tower and cabin, which still exists. There was a later 1934 50-foot L-4 pole whose foundation stones remain.

name: Loneman Lookout
loc:
Glacier National Park 
                    Flathead County, Montana
desc: Loneman Lookout is a 14'x14' lookout similar to Apgar except the catwalk is shored with angle supports. Built in 1930, it is reached by trail from Nyack Ranger Station.

name: Lookout Mountain Lookout
loc:
Bitterroot National Forest 
                    Ravalli County, Montana
desc: Lookout Mountain Lookout on the Bitterroot National Forest is a relative newcomer, having been moved to its current site in 1974, after having been built at Antrim Point only five years earlier. It is an R-6 flattop with catwalk on a 10’ concrete base. Overlooking the upper end of the West Fork of the Bitterroot River, the lookout is regularly staffed during the fire season.

name: McCart Lookout
loc:
Bitterroot National Forest 
                    Ravalli County, Montana
desc: Built by the U.S. Forest Service in 1939, McCart Lookout was completely restored in 1991-92 by the Sula Ranger District of the Bitterroot National Forest in Montana. The structure is an L-4, 14'x14' live-in cab with catwalk on a low wooden tower. It was used for fire detection until 1984 when it was replaced by TeePee Lookout to the north. Located on the edge of the Anaconda Pintler Wilderness and reached only by trail, McCart Lookout was placed in the cabin rental program in 1993 and has proven to be very popular with overnight hikers.

name: McGuire Mountain Lookout
loc:
Kootenai National Forest 
                    Lincoln County, Montana
desc: After 35 years of abandonment, McGuire Mountain Lookout was restored in 1982 and placed in the rental system. The 1924 D-6 cupola lookout was a common design at the time it was constructed. The model was replaced by the L-4s, but a few of them remain as historic sites and only two or three are in fire service nationwide.

name: Meadow Peak Lookout
loc:
Kootenai National Forest 
                    Flathead County, Montana
desc: One of the few Active L-4 lookouts on the Kootenai National Forest, Meadow Mountain is now staffed by the Montana State Division Division of Forestry in cooperation with the U.S. Forest Service which built the structure in 1957. The first people to staff the lookout when it went in service in 1958 were Mr. and Mrs. Dave Griffith. The 14' x 14' cab with catwalk on a 10' wood tower has been well maintained and remains active.

name: Medicine Point Lookout
loc:
Bitterroot National Forest 
                    Ravalli County, Montana
desc: Constructed in 1930 by the CCC, the lookout is located in the Bitterroot Mountains 15 miles south of Darby. It is a 1933 pyramid roof, 14' x 14' L-4 cab with catwalk atop an 8' wood tower. Last staffed in 1976, the lookout was restored in 1999.

name: Mineral Peak Lookout
loc:
Lolo National Forest 
                    Missoula County, Montana
desc: Mineral Peak Lookout lies adjacent to the Rattlesnake Wilderness north of Missoula. The 53’ timber tower is the third on the site. Although built in 1957, the Forest Service topped it with a pre-cut kit model L-4 cab kit in 1936. lt is one of only three remaining 1936-style L-4s on the Lolo National Forest.

name: Minton Peak Lookout
loc:
Kootenai National Forest 
                    Sanders County, Montana
desc: The current Minton Peak Lookout is one of several that have been on this site.  The original 10' pole tower was replaced by an L-4 cab in 1932, then by a new tower in 1968. The present tower was completely rebuilt in 2011.

name: Monument Peak Lookout
loc:
Lewis & Clark National Forest 
                    Meagher County, Montana
desc: The 14'x14' L-4 cab with catwalk was originally placed on a 50' pole tower in 1936. Monument Peak Lookout in the Lewis & Clark National Forest remained active until 1999 when it became unstable and the cab was placed on the ground for restoration. The lookout was rededicated in July 2005 and placed in the rental system as a ground facility.

name: Morrell Lookout
loc:
Lolo National Forest 
                    Powell County, Montana
desc: The first lookout atop 7,796’ Morrell Mountain was a 12’x 12’ log cabin with cupola. Built in 1921, it looks into Montana’s scenic Mission Mountains and expansive timberlands to the south. In 1962 it was replaced with a 15’x 15’ R-6 flattop with catwalk on a 10’ concrete block base. It remains the primary lookout on the Seeley Lake Ranger District of the Lob National Forest.

name: Mount Brown Lookout
loc:
Glacier National Park 
                    Flathead County, Montana
desc:
One of three structures with a short hip roof, Mount Brown Lookout is the oldest remaining lookout in Glacier National Park. It was constructed in 1929. The lookout is reached by a 7-mile trail. 
 From 1949 to 1951, Mount Brown Lookout was manned by lookouts Raymond and Marie Matheny.

name: Mount Henry Lookout
loc:
Kootenai National Forest 
                    Lincoln County, Montana
desc: In 1925 the Kootenai National Forest constructed a stone and frame cupola lookout atop Mount Henry, replacing it with the current L-4 14' x 14' cab with catwalk on a 10' log tower in 1942. Mt. Henry Lookout was abandoned n 1973 but later reactivated as a result of increased fire danger resulting from beetle infestations. Now used only in emergencies, the lookout was partially restored in the 1990s.

name: Northwest Peak Lookout
loc:
Kootenai National Forest 
                    Lincoln County, Montana
desc: Northwest Peak Lookout on the Kootenai National Forest was first used as a patrol camp in 1921. Then in 1929 a prototype gable L-4 ground house was constructed, the forerunner of the classic L-4 model built throughout the west. Abandoned for fire detection in 1955, it survived the elements and was restored in the 1980s as a historic site. Few of the gable roof L-4s remain.

name: Numa Ridge Lookout
loc:
Glacier National Park 
                    Flathead County, Montana
desc: Numa Ridge Lookout is another of the more common 14'x14' designs with an extended hip roof.  Constructed in 1934, it is the most northern lookout in the Park, being only nine miles south of the Canadian border. It is reached by trail from Lake Bowman.

name: Patrick's Knob Lookout
loc:
Lolo National Forest 
                    Sanders County, Montana
desc: In 1976 the R-6 flattop cab with catwalk on a 10’ concrete base became the new Patrick’s Knob Lookout on the Lolo National Forest. It replaced a 20’ pole tower with L-4 cab which has served since 1934 until condemned. For a few years a mobile lookout trailer was used until the new tower was built. Patrick's Knob was named for John W. Patrick, who was the third white man to arrive and settle in the Plains Valley, in 1869. He later ran a ferry boat across the Clark Fork River at Plains. Someone remarked to him that "Yonder mountain seems to be very high," and his answer was, "Oh, that's only a little knob." Thus, "Patrick's Knob", or "Pat's Knob", as it is commonly referred to. Pat's Knob overlooks Plains and the Clark Fork and lower Flathead River drainages. The lookout is still regularly staffed during fire season.

name: Poker Jim Butte Lookout
loc:
Custer National Forest 
                    Rosebud County, Montana
desc: This 30-foot L-4 treated timber lookout was built in 1955. It replaced a previous 1937 lookout.

name: Priscilla Peak Lookout
loc:
Lolo National Forest 
                    Sanders County, Montana
desc: Priscilla Peak Lookout is a shake-walled, gable roof L-2 cupola cabin built in 1929 on the Lolo National Forest and is one of only three remaining of this style in the North Region. Restored and placed on the lookout rental program in 1994, it was withdrawn because of lack of use. Priscilla scans the Thompson River drainage, and has views of the Cabinets, Missions, Swans, and Glacier Park on a clear day.

name: Richards Peak Lookout
loc:
Lolo National Forest 
                    Sanders County, Montana
desc: The first lookout on this site was a D-6 cupola in 1925.  The current Richards Peak Lookout on the Lolo National Forest is an R-6 flattop with catwalk on a 10’ concrete block base and is staffed by the state. Richards Peak was named after the first lookout on the peak, a man by the name of Richards. He was killed in action in France in World War I. Richards Peak lies in the upper Thompson River country.

name: Robinson Mountain Lookout
loc:
Kootenai National Forest 
                    Lincoln County, Montana
desc: There are a few hip roof cupola lookouts remaining, and even fewer gable roof models (although they once were common in Montana and northern Idaho). Robinson Mountain Lookout is one of them.
