Built in 1935, the 100-ft tower, with 8'x8' cab, has been active in watershed and state fire detection ever since.  The Scituate Reservoir lands are closed to public entry, but arrangements can be made for group tours through the Providence Water Supply Board.

name: Acushnet Fire Tower
loc: Bristol County, Massachusetts
admin: Mass. Bureau of Forest Fire Control
desc: Acushnet Lookout was constructed by the CCC in 1937 replacing a tower dating to 1918. The 60’ Aermotor tower with 10’x10’ wooden cab is operated by the Massachusetts Bureau of Forest Fire Control.
agency: Mass. Bureau of Forest Fire Co

name: Agawam Fire Tower
loc:
Town of Agawam 
                    Hamden County, Massachusetts
admin: Mass. Bureau of Forest Fire Control
desc: Located in Hamden County, Agawam Lookout is a 10’x10’ wooden cab on a 70’ steel tower built in 1959. It replaced an earlier 48’ tower built in 1920.
agency: Mass. Bureau of Forest Fire Co

name: Andover Fire Tower
loc:
Town of Andover 
                    Essex County, Massachusetts
admin: Mass. Bureau of Forest Fire Control
desc: The third of four towers built in Essex County in 1924, Andover Fire Tower was replaced in 1970. The 68' steel tower with a 10'x10' wooden cab is operated by the Bureau of Fire Control of the Massachusetts Department of Conservation and Recreation. All of this group of fire towers in Massachusetts are in active service.
agency: Mass. Bureau of Forest Fire Co

name: Barnstable Fire Tower
loc:
Clay Hill 
                    Barnstable County, Massachusetts
admin: Mass. Bureau of Forest Fire Control
desc: The first fire lookout in Barnstable County on Cape Cod was staffed in 1912 on a wooden tower built by donors on Shoot Flying Hill in 1897.  A steel tower was built in 1912 and stood until 1947.  The present Barnstable Lookout was constructed by the MA Bureau of Forest Fire Control in that year.  It is a 68’ steel tower with 10’x10’ wooden cab.
agency: Mass. Bureau of Forest Fire Co

name: Bourne Fire Tower
loc:
Town of Bourne 
                    Barnstable County, Massachusetts
admin: Mass. Bureau of Forest Fire Control
desc: The present Bourne Fire Tower is a 70’ steel tower with standard Mass.10’x10’ wood cab was built in 1947 replacing a 48’ tower built in 1913.   This is the second tower built in Barnstable County and the 23rd state tower built overall. It is operated by the Massachusetts Bureau of Forest Fire Control.
agency: Mass. Bureau of Forest Fire Co

name: Brewster Fire Tower
loc:
Deer Park Hill 
                    Barnstable County, Massachusetts
admin: Mass. Bureau of Forest Fire Control
desc: The Massachusetts Bureau of Fire Control built the Brewster Fire Tower on Cape Cod in 1949.  It is a 68’ steel tower with a 10’x10’cab.
agency: Mass. Bureau of Forest Fire Co

name: Brimfield Fire Tower
loc:
Steerage Rock 
                    Hampden County, Massachusetts
desc: Located on Steerage Rock, Brimfield tower has provided decades of service to Massachusetts.

name: Carver Fire Tower
loc:
Bare Hill 
                    Plymouth County, Massachusetts
admin: Mass. Bureau of Forest Fire Control
desc: The tallest and largest lookout in Massachusetts, the 80’ tubular steel Carver Fire Tower has a unique slant window cab without a door to the catwalk!  Built in 1988, it is the third to overlook this section of the Miles Standish State Forest.
agency: Mass. Bureau of Forest Fire Co

name: Charlton Fire Tower
loc:
Town of Charlton 
                    Worcester County, Massachusetts
admin: Mass. Bureau of Forest Fire Control
desc: Constructed in 1939 by the CCC, Charlton Fire Tower is a 60’ Aermotor steel tower with a “perched” 10’x10’ wood cab.  The site was first used for fire detection in 1914 as a bare knob secondary station atop Little Mugget hill. The first tower was a 48’ structure built in 1917.   It was destroyed in the Great Hurricane of 1938.
agency: Mass. Bureau of Forest Fire Co

name: Chelmsford Fire Tower
loc:
Robbins Hill 
                    Middlesex County, Massachusetts
admin: Mass. Bureau of Forest Fire Control
desc: The 68’ Chelmsford Fire Tower with a 10’x10’ wooden cab was constructed by Mass. BFC in 1938. It is the fourth tower to be constructed on the site, including one that was destroyed by the hurricane of 1938.
agency: Mass. Bureau of Forest Fire Co

name: Chester Fire Tower
loc:
Town of Chester 
                    Hampden County, Massachusetts
admin: Mass. Bureau of Forest Fire Control
desc: Built by the CCC in 1934 for the Massachusetts Bureau of Fire Control, Chester Fire Tower is located on Holcomb Hill in Hampden County. The site was first used as a temporary lookout station in 1915. A one acre tract was purchased in 1918 and a 40’ wood tower erected. It was replaced 26 years later with the current 60’ steel tower. A larger 10’x10’ aluminum cab (the Mass. Standard cab) was installed in 1965.
agency: Mass. Bureau of Forest Fire Co

name: Dennis Fire Tower
loc:
Town of Dennis 
                    Barnstable County, Massachusetts
admin: Mass. Bureau of Forest Fire Control
desc: The last tower built on Cape Cod, Dennis Fire Tower was constructed in 1947. The 65' steel tower with 10'x10' cab completes the detection coverage of the fire prone cape.
agency: Mass. Bureau of Forest Fire Co

name: Fall River Fire Tower
loc:
City of Fall River 
                    Bristol County, Massachusetts
admin: Mass. Bureau of Forest Fire Control
desc: Fall River Fire Tower was constructed by the Mass. Bureau of Fire Control in 1966.   The 75’ steel tower with 10’x10’ wood cab replace a similar 60’ structure built in 1914 on nearby Copicut Hill.
agency: Mass. Bureau of Forest Fire Co

name: Falmouth Fire Tower
loc:
Town of Falmouth 
                    Barnstable County, Massachusetts
admin: Mass. Bureau of Forest Fire Control
desc: The 68' Falmouth Fire Tower with a 10'x10' cab was constructed in 1947. It replaced a 40' steel tower built in 1914 at the request of local officials. This tower covers southern upper Cape Cod including part of Otis Air Force Base.
agency: Mass. Bureau of Forest Fire Co

name: Georgetown Fire Tower
loc:
Town of Georgetown 
                    Essex County, Massachusetts
admin: Mass. Bureau of Forest Fire Control
desc: The Georgetown Fire Tower has an unusual cab with a catwalk on the roof.  The 70’ tower with 10'x10' cab was built in 1969 by the Mass. Bureau of Forest Fire Control replacing a 40’ tower on nearby Baldpate Hill built in 1917. The first tower in that location was a unique 30’ tower with a spiral staircase and a 12’x12’ cab in use through 1937.
agency: Mass. Bureau of Forest Fire Co

name: Goshen Fire Tower
loc:
D.A.R. State Forest 
                    Hampshire County, Massachusetts
admin: Mass. Bureau of Forest Fire Control
desc: Located on the D.A.R. State Forest, Goshen Lookout was constructed in 1952. It sits on the eastern edge of the Berkshire Mountains and filled the last major gap in the statewide detection grid.
agency: Mass. Bureau of Forest Fire Co

name: Groton Fire Tower
loc:
Town of Groton 
                    Middlesex County, Massachusetts
admin: Mass. Bureau of Forest Fire Control
desc: Groton Fire Tower was built in 1957. It is a 68' steel tower with a 10'x10' wooden cab, and a smaller cab below. The first tower on this site was a 70' wooden tower furnished by the USFS in 1941.
agency: Mass. Bureau of Forest Fire Co

name: Hanson Fire Tower
loc:
Town of Hanson 
                    Plymouth County, Massachusetts
admin: Mass. Bureau of Forest Fire Control
desc: The first tower on this site was a 48' steel structure. Due to rapid tree growth, it was moved in 1920 to Pelham and replaced with a 68' tower. The present Hanson Fire Tower is a 70' steel tower with 10'x10' cab built in 1969 on 150' Bonney Hill near Plymouth, MA.
agency: Mass. Bureau of Forest Fire Co

name: Harvard Fire Tower
loc:
Town of Harvard 
                    Worcester County, Massachusetts
admin: Mass. Bureau of Forest Fire Control
desc: Harvard Fire Tower is a 70' steel tower with 10'x10' cab overlooking the Harvard Forest. It replaced a 68' tower built in 1921.
agency: Mass. Bureau of Forest Fire Co

name: Kingston Fire Tower
loc:
Town of Kingston 
                    Plymouth County, Massachusetts
admin: Mass. Bureau of Forest Fire Control
desc: The first Kingston Fire Tower was a 38' structure built in 1916 as a replacement for the Plymouth tower. However, it was decided instead to move that tower nearby and keep both in service. The present 75' steel tower with 10'x10' cab was constructed in 1956.
agency: Mass. Bureau of Forest Fire Co

name: Lenox Fire Tower
loc:
Lenox Mountain 
                    Berkshire County, Massachusetts
desc: n 1915, a 48' tower was erected atop Lenox mountain and the towns of Lenox, Richmond, and Pittsfield donated $200 toward the purchase of this tower. Two miles of phone line had to be constructed to this tower. In 1952, the state bought the land under the tower and the right of way. In 1963, the tower was temporarily closed due to the poor condition of the tower and In 1966, a new 75' tower with a 10'x10' cab and new fence was built. After the new tower was built, it was dedicated and renamed in the memory of past Chief of Fire Control "Hutchinson", who at the time of his death was the oldest chief in years of service and age. In 1970, this tower blew over in a high wind storm.   In the fall of 1970, the current 68' tower was built. The tower was last staffed during the 1988 fire season. In the winter of 1995, the tower cab and stairs were destroyed by fire.   As of 2015, the tower's frame remains and is used to host communiations equipment. This tower is now listed on the  Former Fire Lookout Sites page .

name: Ludlow Fire Tower
loc:
Ludlow State Forest 
                    Hampden County, Massachusetts
admin: Mass. Bureau of Forest Fire Control
desc: Located on Minechoag Mountain just east of Springfield, Ludlow Fire Tower is easily seen from the Massachusetts Turnpike. In 1936 the 50 acre Ludlow State Forest was purchased and tower construction begun by the CCC. The original 7’x7’ metal cab on the 60’ steel tower was replaced in 1967 with the Mass. 10’x10’ aluminum cab which was upgraded again in 1999. An urban/interface tower, it is in active service.
agency: Mass. Bureau of Forest Fire Co

name: Macallester Fire Tower
loc:
Dover Land Trust Reserve 
                    Norfolk County, Massachusetts
admin: Mass. Bureau of Forest Fire Control
desc: Originally known as Dover Tower, the lookout was renamed in honor of Ralph W. MacAllester in 1993.  The site has been used for fire detection since 1939.  The present 60' steel tower was erected in 1953.
agency: Mass. Bureau of Forest Fire Co

name: Manchester Fire Tower
loc:
Town of Manchester 
                    Essex County, Massachusetts
admin: Mass. Bureau of Forest Fire Control
desc: Owing to the number of fires in the area in 1913, the North Shore improvement association donated seven acres of land and $400 for the construction of Manchester Fire Tower. In 1968 it was replaced by this 68' tower with 10'x10' cab.
agency: Mass. Bureau of Forest Fire Co

name: Mendon Fire Tower
loc:
Town of Mendon 
                    Worcester County, Massachusetts
admin: Mass. Bureau of Forest Fire Control
desc: The first Mendon Fire Tower was placed into operation in 1916 to cover southern Worcester County and triangulate with lookouts in northern Rhode Island. The present 70' steel tower with 10'x10' cab was built in 1955.
agency: Mass. Bureau of Forest Fire Co

name: Middleboro Fire Tower
loc:
Town of Middleboro 
                    Plymouth County, Massachusetts
admin: Mass. Bureau of Forest Fire Control
desc: The first Middleboro Lookout was located in the Middleboro Town Hall observatory room. It was replaced in 1913 when a new 48' tower was erected on Barden's Hill. The present 75' steel tower with 10'x10' cab was constructed in 1966.
agency: Mass. Bureau of Forest Fire Co

name: Milton Fire Tower
loc:
Great Blue Hill 
                    Norfolk County, Massachusetts
admin: Mass. Department of Conservation and Recreation, Urban Parks Division
desc: The Milton Fire Tower on the Great Blue Hill Reservation south of Boston is certainly one of a kind. Built in 1885 as a weather observatory, it was the fourth fire lookout operated by the state and was active from 1911-1915.

name: Monterey Fire Tower
loc:
Town of Monterey 
                    Berkshire County, Massachusetts
admin: Mass. Bureau of Forest Fire Control
desc: Built in 1935, Monterey Fire Tower is a 60' steel structure with a "perched" 10'x10' wooden cab. It was the first tower built in Berkshire County by the Civilian Conservation Corps (CCC).
agency: Mass. Bureau of Forest Fire Co

name: Mount Washington Fire Tower at Mount Everett
loc:
Mount Everett State Reservation 
                    Berkshire County, Massachusetts
admin: Massachusetts Bureau of Forest Fire Control
desc:
The first lookout on this site was a 38' tower with 10' x 10' cab erected in 1915. The states of Massachusetts, Connecticut, and New York contributed to its funding, as did the town of Great Barrington with a $150 contribution. The tower was rebuilt in 1945 and a new 40' tower constructed in 1970. It was staffed until 1972. 
  This tower was removed in 2003 due to disputes with the town officials. The tower was sold to a private landowner in the same town.

name: North Attleboro Fire Tower
loc:
Town of North Attleboro 
                    Bristol County, Massachusetts
admin: Mass. Bureau of Forest Fire Control

When the state took over fire detection in 1911 they built a new tower on Reservoir Hill. In 1939, a replacement 48’ tower was relocated on Telegraph Hill and served until 1942. name: Westborough Fire Tower
loc:
Fay Mountain 
                    Worcester County, Massachusetts
desc:
Located on top of Fay Mountain, a fire tower has been on this site since 1911 when a 38-foot tower with an 8'-by-8' cab was built.  It was replaced in 1915 with a new 68-foot tower sporting a 10'-by-10' cab; the old tower was moved to Chester. This tower was destroyed in the great hurricane of 1938 and replaced by a temporary tower. In 1939, a new 68-foot steel tower was built.
 

 
The 1939 tower was eventually replaced when the US Army which built a radar tower on the site. After the radar was discontinued in 1970, Massachusetts built a new cab on top of the three-legged radar tower. Use of this site was discontinued in 1982, at which time the tower was transferred to the city of Westboro and eventually to a private landowner. Today, the fire cab has been replaced by a platform used to mount communication antennas.
 

 
This was one of the only two three-legged towers built in Massachusetts.

name: Mount Nonotuck Lookout Tower
loc:
Mount Tom State Reservation 
                    Hampden County, Massachusetts
desc:
At the northern section of the Mt. Tom State Reservation in Holyoke Massachusetts is Mt. Nonotuck (827'), a subsidiary peak. This area is known for the Eyrie House Ruins. The tower sits above the ruins at elevation 950' It is accessible by trail off Reservation Road. At the top are views of the Connecticut River Valley, including the Oxbow.  
  In 1861 the Eyrie House Hotel was built here as a vacation destination, a popular Summit House such as the one still standing across the Connecticut River on Skinner Mountain. Forty years later it burned down due to a fire started for horse cremation. There are stone ruins of the stable and hotel pavilion as well as other remnants of the buildings in the area surrounding the lookout tower. The tower was not part of the hotel. The Tower itself is steel construction with red paint. It has a narrow base about 8' square. The stairs to the top are very steep - nearly a ladder. At the top is a wide platform that cantilevers off the frame. At the base of the tower is a small derelict shed. This tower is not as well maintained as its neighbors on Goat Peak and the Bray Tower both on the Mt. Tom Reservation, but its local history, incredible views, and steep ascent make it an exciting addition to a local Lookout Tower adventure.  
  The photo is from December 2025.

name: Bray Lookout Tower
loc:
Mount Tom State Reservation 
                    Hampshire County, Massachusetts
desc:
Bray Tower is the most easily accessible tower on the Mt. Tom State Reservation in Holyoke Massachusetts. You can drive right up to it, by taking Christopher Clark Road from the west, in Easthampton, or by Reservation Road from the east in Holyoke. Once you reach the pavilion with the playground, take the western branch of Christopher Clark Road straight to Bray Tower.  
  Bray Tower is one of two official lookout towers in the Mount Tom State Reservation. It is very similar to the Goat Peak Tower built in 1928. It is about 42' tall with a 15.5 square base and 10' square platform. It is steel and painted green. The tower is still used as a place to observe the annual hawk and other raptor migration.  
 Photo taken in  March 2026

name: Goat Peak Lookout Tower
loc:
Mount Tom State Reservation 
                    Hampden County, Massachusetts
desc:
The Goat Peak Lookout Tower is on the north-western side of the Mount Tom State Reservation in Holyoke Massachusetts. It is accessible by several trails branching off Reservation Road, which bisects the forest. Goat Peak (822') is a subsidiary peak of Mt. Tom (1,202'). At the top are views of Easthampton to the West, and the Seven Sisters range on Skinner State Park and UMass Amherst to the North.  
  Goat Peak Lookout tower was built in 1928 and is still maintained to this day. It is about 42' feet tall with a 15.5' base. The steel frame rests atop four concrete bollards. It is painted green. The viewing platform is a 10' square and is reached by three sets of stairs. The platform floor was recently replaced with fresh lumber as of 2025. The tower is currently used for recreational viewing, and for witnessing the annual southern hawk migration each fall.  
  Goat Peak Lookout Tower December 2025
